name: Aberdeen

caz.name: Aberdeen Low Emission Zone
caz.scope: It covers the city centre and issues penalty charges to vehicles that do not meet its standards.

intro: Privately kept diesel cars in the Aberdeen City council area fell from 22,077 to 19,715 in the year to June 2026, a drop of 10.7%. That is the steepest fall of the 104 large towns we cover, and diesel is now 21.3% of private cars there, against 63.5% on petrol. If you are keeping your diesel rather than replacing it, Stage 1 remapping is one way to get more from the engine you already have. It is a software change to the fuel, boost and timing settings, kept within the engine's limits, and nothing is bolted on. The gain most diesel drivers notice is mid-range torque: easier overtaking, smoother joins onto faster roads and fewer downshifts.
driving: The Aberdeen Low Emission Zone covers the city centre and applies to both cars and vans, enforced by a penalty charge rather than a fee to enter. A remap does not change a vehicle's emissions standard, so it makes no difference to whether the zone applies to yours. The A96, A92, A93 and A944 are among the main roads, and the nearest service area, Stracathro on the A90, is 51.5 km away. In 2025 MOT tests across AB postcodes, the Volkswagen Golf and Land Rover Discovery were the most tested diesel cars, and the Ford Transit led the vans ahead of the Volkswagen Transporter. For a Discovery with a trailer or a loaded Transit on a long A-road run, extra mid-range torque is what you feel.

name: Barking and Dagenham
intro: None of the 104 large towns we cover held on to its diesel cars better than Barking and Dagenham. Privately kept diesel cars in the council area went from 12,085 to 11,907 in the year to the end of June 2026, a fall of only 1.5%. Diesel still makes up about 19% of the 61,484 private cars there. Diesels are leaving the road slowly here, and for owners who plan to keep one, Stage 1 remapping is a way to get more from it. It is a software change to the engine's fuel, boost and timing settings, kept within the engine's limits, with nothing bolted on. On a diesel, the gain most people notice is mid-range torque: easier overtaking and smoother joins onto fast roads.
driving: In the 2021 Census, 32.5% of working residents in the Barking and Dagenham council area drove to work, well below the England and Wales figure of 45.1%, while 25.6% travelled 10 km or more, above the England and Wales figure of 19%. The nearest service area is Moto Thurrock on the M25, about 11 km away. The council area also has 2,967 privately kept vans, 95.1% of them diesel, and in 2025 MOT tests across RM postcodes the Ford Transit was the most tested diesel van. For a loaded Transit, a remap's extra torque helps, within gearbox and clutch limits. The London ULEZ covers every borough and can charge cars and vans. A remap doesn't change a vehicle's emissions standard, so it won't change whether you pay.

name: Barnet
intro: Barnet sits 7th of the 104 large towns we cover for plug-in cars, which make up 9% of the 130,542 privately kept cars in the council area. Diesel, at 12.4%, is one of the lowest shares in the same group. Both figures are for the end of June 2026. If yours is one of the diesels still on Barnet's roads, a Stage 1 remap changes how it drives, not what it runs on. The engine's settings are adjusted in software, inside its limits, and the extra mid-range torque shows when you overtake or join a fast road. Any change in fuel use depends on how you drive, so treat it as a side effect, not the reason.
driving: The M1, A1, A41 and A406 are among Barnet's main roads. London Gateway Services on the M1 is 4.4 km away and South Mimms on the A1(M) is 8.2 km, so a run out of London starts close by. In the 2021 Census, 25.1% of working residents in the Barnet council area drove to work, against 45.1% across England and Wales, and 29.9% of households had no car. In 2025 MOT tests across NW postcodes, the Mercedes-Benz E Class was the most tested diesel car and the Ford Transit the most tested diesel van. The ULEZ covers every London borough, and its daily charge can apply to cars and vans. A remap does not change a vehicle's emissions standard, so it does not change whether that charge applies.

name: Basildon
intro: Long journeys to work stand out in the Basildon figures. In the 2021 Census, 7.4% of working residents in the Basildon built-up area travelled 30 km or more in a straight line, against 4.4% across England and Wales, and 21.8% travelled at least 10 km. Those figures come from a lockdown census day, so commuting was lower than usual. For a diesel that covers that kind of distance, Stage 1 remapping is mostly about how the engine pulls at speed: more mid-range torque for overtaking and joining fast roads, and less need to change down. Nothing is bolted on. The remap adjusts fuel, boost and timing settings, within the engine's limits.
driving: The main part of Basildon sits between two dual carriageways, the A127 to the north and the A13 to the south, and Orsett Cock Services on the A13 is 7.3 km away. In the 2021 Census, 48.7% of working residents in the built-up area drove to work, above the England and Wales figure of 45.1%. At the end of June 2026 the Basildon council area had 89,209 privately kept cars, 24.3% diesel and 62.2% petrol, and 6,739 private vans, 94% of them diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across SS postcodes, the Ford Kuga was the most tested diesel car and the Ford Transit the most tested diesel van. On a loaded van, Stage 1 adds mid-range pull, within what the clutch and gearbox can handle.

name: Basingstoke
intro: Two-car households are common in Basingstoke. In the 2021 Census, 40.9% of households in the Basingstoke built-up area had two or more cars, well above the England and Wales figure of 35.4%, and only 17.8% had none, against 23.3%. More cars per home means more choice over which one does the long runs, carries the load or tows, and that is usually the one worth looking at for Stage 1 remapping. The work is a software change to the engine's fuel, boost and timing settings, within its limits, with nothing bolted on. On a diesel the gain you feel is mid-range torque, so the car pulls cleanly from low revs and needs fewer downshifts.
driving: The M3 is among Basingstoke's main roads, with the A339, A33 and A30, and the closest service area is Popham on the A303, 11.9 km away. In the 2021 Census, 5.2% of working residents in the built-up area travelled 30 km or more to work, against 4.4% across England and Wales. In the Basingstoke and Deane council area, 28.3% of privately kept cars were diesel at the end of June 2026, and their number fell 7% over the year, one of the steepest falls of the 104 large towns we cover. In 2025 MOT tests across RG postcodes, the BMW 3 Series and Mercedes-Benz E Class were among the most tested diesel cars. On cars like these, a remap mainly means easier overtaking and smoother joins onto the M3.

name: Belfast
intro: Belfast drivers have been slow to plug in. Only 2.7% of privately kept cars in the council area were plug-ins at the end of June 2026, the lowest share of the 104 large towns we cover. Diesel goes the other way: at 36.9%, Belfast has the 3rd highest diesel share of the 104, which comes to 45,030 private diesel cars. Where diesel is still the everyday car, Stage 1 remapping is a practical way to make one more pleasant to drive. Fuel, boost and timing are adjusted in the engine software, the changes stay inside the engine's limits, and no parts are added. What you feel is mid-range pull: overtaking with less effort and fewer downshifts when the road climbs.
driving: In the 2021 Census, 47.2% of working residents in the Belfast council area drove to work, but only 8.8% travelled 10 km or more, and a third of households, 33.9%, had no car. Lisburn Services on the M1 is about 9 km away, and Applegreen Temple Patrick Services Northbound on the M2 about 12 km. The diesel count is falling slowly, down 2.8% over the year to June 2026, one of the smallest falls of the 104. The council area also has 5,847 privately kept vans, 97.5% of them diesel. A van that works loaded gains useful torque from a remap, though its gearbox and clutch still set the limits. If an AdBlue, DPF or EGR fault is showing, that is repaired before any remap.

name: Bexley
intro: Seven in ten privately kept cars in the Bexley council area run on petrol: 70.8% of 98,067 at the end of June 2026. Diesel makes up 13.5%, one of the lowest shares among the 104 large towns we cover, and private diesel cars fell from 14,230 to 13,259 over the year, one of the steepest drops in that group. So a Stage 1 remap here is often a petrol question as well as a diesel one. The principle is the same on both: software settings for fuel, boost and timing are changed within the engine's limits, and no parts are added. On the diesels that remain, the gain you notice most is mid-range pull.
driving: The A2 and A13 are among Bexley's main roads, and the nearest listed service area is Moto Thurrock on the M25, 9 km away, with Tollgate on the A2 at 15.9 km. In the 2021 Census, 36% of working residents in the Bexley council area drove to work and 32.3% of households had two or more cars. The council area has 4,772 privately kept vans, 90.9% of them diesel, and the Ford Transit was the most tested diesel van in 2025 MOT tests across DA postcodes. On a loaded van, extra torque helps, within gearbox and clutch limits. Bexley is inside the ULEZ, where a daily charge can apply to cars and vans, and a remap leaves the emissions standard as it was, so it does not change that.

name: Birkenhead
intro: A third of households in the Birkenhead built-up area had no car in the 2021 Census: 33.1%, against 23.3% for England and Wales. Yet 51% of working residents drove to work, so the cars that are owned on this side of the Mersey tend to be used every day. That was a lockdown census day, so read it as a snapshot. For a diesel in daily use, Stage 1 remapping changes the mid-range, which is where it pulls out of junctions, climbs and joins faster roads. A remap is no cure for a fault, though: any DPF or EGR problem is repaired first.
driving: The M53 is the only motorway on Birkenhead's main road list, with the A41, A552 and A554 among the A roads, and Wallasey is 3.6 km away. The closest listed service area, Earlsfield Services on the M57, is 16.1 km off. Across the Wirral council area there were 149,775 privately kept cars at the end of June 2026, 28.4% of them diesel, and private diesel cars fell from 45,221 to 42,551 over the year. Private vans numbered 10,454, and 95.5% were diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across CH postcodes, the Volkswagen Golf was the most tested diesel car and the Ford Transit the most tested diesel van. Loaded vans feel Stage 1 torque most, and an insurer must be told about any remap.

name: Birmingham

caz.name: Birmingham Clean Air Zone
caz.scope: It covers the city centre inside the A4540 Middleway and applies to cars and vans.

intro: Birmingham's Clean Air Zone is a Class D charging zone covering the city centre inside the A4540 Middleway ring road, though not the Middleway itself, and it applies to both cars and vans. Inside the zone or out of it, Stage 1 remapping on a diesel is felt as mid-range torque: joining the M6 or the A38(M) from a slip road and overtaking on the A45 become noticeably easier. The change is to the fuel, boost and timing settings, within the engine's limits. It does not alter the emissions standard, so a car or van the zone charges today is charged after a remap too, and one it does not charge stays that way.
driving: At the end of June 2026 the Birmingham council area had 411,153 privately kept cars. Only 3.6% were plug-ins, one of the lowest shares of the 104 large towns we cover, and 27.1% were diesel, about 111,000 cars. In the 2021 Census, 32.9% of households in the Birmingham built-up area had no car, above the England and Wales figure of 23.3%, yet 46.2% of working residents drove to work. In 2025 MOT tests across B postcodes, the Ford Transit and Mercedes-Benz Sprinter were the most tested diesel vans, with the Volkswagen Golf and BMW 3 Series top among cars. A loaded Sprinter or Transit gains stronger pull at low revs from Stage 1, though the gearbox and clutch limits still set how far a van's remap should go.

name: Blackburn
intro: Blackburn with Darwen has the 2nd highest share of diesel cars of the 104 large towns we cover. At the end of June 2026, 38.5% of the council area's 64,075 privately kept cars ran on diesel, and their number had fallen by only 2.1% in a year, one of the smallest drops of the 104. With that many diesels in daily use, the order of work matters. A diesel with a DPF, EGR or injector fault is repaired first, and Stage 1 remapping comes after, once the engine is healthy. The remap then lifts mid-range torque, which is where a diesel does its everyday work: overtaking, hills and joining faster roads.
driving: ExtraMSA Blackburn with Darwen Services, on the M65, is under 4 km from the town, and the A666, A677 and A59 are among its main roads. In the 2021 Census, 55.6% of working residents in the Blackburn built-up area drove to work, well above the England and Wales figure of 45.1%. The council area has 4,039 privately kept vans, 96.6% of them diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across BB postcodes, the Volkswagen Golf was the most tested diesel car by a wide margin, and the Ford Transit led the diesel vans, with the Mercedes-Benz Sprinter and Volkswagen Transporter behind. A remap gives a Golf easier pace on the M65 and a loaded van more torque, within gearbox and clutch limits.

name: Blackpool
intro: Blackpool keeps more vans per car than most of the towns we cover: 90 privately kept vans for every 1,000 private cars in the council area, the 7th highest ratio of the 104. That came to 5,007 vans at the end of June 2026, and 96.1% of them run on diesel. For a van, a Stage 1 remap is mostly about torque. With more pull from low revs, a loaded van or one towing a trailer holds its gear longer and needs fewer downshifts. Gearbox and clutch limits still matter, so the remap file has to be matched to the vehicle rather than chosen for the biggest possible gain.
driving: The M55 is the only motorway on Blackpool's list of main roads, alongside A-roads such as the A583 and A584, and the nearest listed service area, Lancaster on the M6, is 24.9 km away. Commutes were short in the 2021 Census: only 10.4% of working residents in the Blackpool built-up area travelled 10 km or more to work, against 19% across England and Wales, although 49.9% drove. Lytham St Anne's is 5.3 km away and Poulton-le-Fylde 6.4 km. Of the 55,696 private cars in the council area, 32.1% are diesel and only 3.2% plug-in, one of the lowest plug-in shares of the 104. In 2025 MOT tests across FY postcodes, the BMW 3 Series was the most tested diesel car. Any DPF or other fault is repaired before a remap.

name: Bolton
intro: At the end of June 2026, 38,380 privately kept cars in the Bolton council area ran on diesel, 30.1% of the 127,512 total and down from 40,395 a year earlier. That is still a large pool of cars for which Stage 1 remapping is worth a look. Bolton sits in the foothills of the West Pennine Moors, so climbs come with ordinary driving, and the change most diesel owners notice is in the mid-range: fewer downshifts on hills, easier overtaking and a calmer pull with passengers or a trailer. The work is software only, adjusting fuel, boost and timing within the engine's limits.
driving: Rivington Services on the M61 is 9.3 km away, and the A666, A673, A58 and A6 are on the main road list. In the 2021 Census, 52.9% of working residents in the Bolton built-up area drove to work, well above 45.1% for England and Wales, but only 2% travelled 30 km or more, so most commutes were local. Petrol cars made up 53.8% of the council area's privately kept cars and petrol hybrids 11.1%. The 8,184 private vans were 96.6% diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across BL postcodes, the Ford Transit led the diesel vans ahead of the Mercedes-Benz Sprinter, and the Volkswagen Golf led the cars. On a working van, Stage 1 torque helps with a load, provided the clutch and gearbox are in good order.

name: Bournemouth
intro: For every 1,000 privately kept cars in the Bournemouth, Christchurch and Poole council area there are 97 privately kept vans, the second highest ratio of the 104 large towns we cover. That came to 18,848 private vans at the end of June 2026, and 94.2% of them run on diesel. A van that spends the day loaded, or pulling a trailer, is where Stage 1 remapping makes the clearest difference. Only the software changes: the fuel, boost and timing settings, kept within the engine's limits. Extra mid-range torque means easier pulling away and fewer downshifts with weight on board, while the gearbox and clutch decide how far a van's remap should sensibly go.
driving: Commutes around Bournemouth were short in the 2021 Census: only 10.5% of working residents in the built-up area travelled 10 km or more to work, against 19% across England and Wales. Poole is 5.8 km away and Christchurch 9.1 km, and the main roads include the A338, A35, A3049 and A348. The nearest service area, Picket Post on the A31, is 16.2 km out. In 2025 MOT tests across BH postcodes, the Volkswagen Transporter was the most tested diesel van, ahead of the Ford Transit, and the Volkswagen Golf led the diesel cars. Of the council area's 194,180 private cars, 27.5% are diesel. On short runs the useful part of a remap is low-rev pull, and any diesel with a DPF fault is repaired before it is remapped.

name: Bradford

caz.name: Bradford Clean Air Zone
caz.scope: It covers Bradford city centre and the outer ring road area and charges vans, not private cars.

intro: Bradford's Clean Air Zone, which covers the city centre and the outer ring road area, can charge vans but does not charge private cars. If you run a diesel van in the city, one point is worth knowing first: a remap does not change a vehicle's emissions standard, so it won't change whether the zone charges it. What Stage 1 remapping does change is how the engine responds. Nothing on the van is replaced: the fuel, boost and timing settings are changed in software, within the engine's limits. The extra mid-range torque helps when you are loaded or towing, while the gearbox and clutch decide how far it can go. A van with a DPF, AdBlue or EGR fault is repaired first.
driving: Diesel is unusually common in the Bradford council area: 36.4% of privately kept cars, one of the highest shares of the 104 large towns we cover, and their number fell only 1.6% over the year to June 2026. Main roads include the M606, A6177 and A658, and the nearest service area is Welcome Break Hartshead Moor on the M62, about 9 km away. In the 2021 Census, 50.4% of working residents in the Bradford built-up area drove to work. In 2025 MOT tests across BD postcodes, the Volkswagen Golf was by far the most tested diesel car, with the Audi A3 and BMW 3 Series next. On cars like these, a remap is about stronger pull through the gears and easier motorway joins.

name: Brent
intro: Diesel is hanging on in Brent. Privately kept diesel cars in the Brent council area went from 12,884 to 12,516 in the year to June 2026, a fall of 2.9% and the 8th smallest among the 104 large towns we cover. Diesel still accounts for 15.3% of the 82,039 private cars here. If you are keeping a diesel, a Stage 1 remap is one way to get more out of it without fitting anything. The gain you feel most is in the mid-range: more pull at the revs you actually use, so fewer changes down a gear. Your insurer has to be told about the remap.
driving: The M1, A406, A40 and A41 all appear among Brent's main roads, and London Gateway Services on the M1 is 8.1 km away. In the 2021 Census, 44.1% of households in the Brent council area had no car, and 21.7% of working residents drove to work, against 45.1% across England and Wales. In the council area, plug-ins make up 8.1% of private cars, one of the highest shares of the 104, and 92.8% of the 3,386 private vans are diesel, and in 2025 MOT tests across HA postcodes the Ford Transit was the most tested diesel van. As for the ULEZ, which can charge both cars and vans, a remap has no effect, because it does not alter a vehicle's emissions standard.

name: Brighton and Hove
intro: For every 1,000 privately kept cars in the Brighton and Hove council area at the end of June 2026, there were 92 private vans, the 4th highest ratio of the 104 large towns we cover. Of those 8,112 vans, 92.8% were diesel. If you run one of them, think about Stage 1 remapping in terms of the load you carry. The extra torque sits in the mid-range, so a van that is often full or towing does more of its work without the driver reaching for a lower gear. Before any remap, the clutch and gearbox need to be in good order, because they set the limits.
driving: The A23 and A27 head the main road list, with the A259 and A270 alongside them, and Pyecombe Services on the A23 is 7.9 km away. Lewes is 8.5 km off. In the 2021 Census, only 25% of working residents in the built-up area drove to work, against 45.1% for England and Wales, and 37.5% of households had no car. The council area had 87,807 privately kept cars at the end of June 2026, 63.3% petrol and 23.9% diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across BN postcodes, the Volkswagen Golf was the most tested diesel car, while the Ford Transit and Volkswagen Transporter led the vans. For a car that uses the A23 or A27, Stage 1 makes joining faster traffic and overtaking easier.

name: Bristol

caz.name: Bristol Clean Air Zone
caz.scope: It covers a small area of central Bristol and applies to cars and vans.

intro: Only 32% of working residents in the Bristol built-up area drove to work in the 2021 Census, far below the England and Wales figure of 45.1%. Diesel is thinning out too. In the Bristol council area, privately kept diesel cars fell 7.1% in the year to June 2026, one of the steepest falls of the 104 large towns we cover, and diesel is now 19.4% of private cars. For the diesels that stay, Stage 1 remapping is a software job only: the fuel, boost and timing settings are changed within the engine's limits and nothing is bolted on. Most of the gain sits in the mid-range, which suits pulling away with a load or joining the M32.
driving: Bristol's Clean Air Zone, a Class D charging zone, covers a small area of central Bristol and applies to cars and vans. A remap does not alter a vehicle's emissions standard, so it does not change whether the zone charges it. Vans are common: the council area had 88 privately kept vans per 1,000 private cars at the end of June 2026, the 8th highest ratio of the 104 large towns we cover, and 94.2% of its 15,784 vans were diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across BS postcodes, the Ford Transit and Volkswagen Transporter were the most tested diesel vans. The nearest service area, Gordano on the M5, is 8.7 km away. For a working van, the torque gain helps most when loaded, within what the clutch can handle.

name: Bromley
intro: Petrol accounts for 70.6% of the 137,106 privately kept cars in the Bromley council area, and diesel for just 12.2%, one of the lowest diesel shares of the 104 large towns we cover. So in Bromley, Stage 1 remapping is more often about a petrol car than a diesel. The method is the same on both: the remap adjusts the fuel, boost and timing settings rather than adding parts, and stays within the engine's limits. On a petrol the result is a stronger, smoother response through the middle of the rev range. On a diesel it is more torque for overtaking and joining fast roads. Your insurer needs to be told either way.
driving: The council area has 6,181 privately kept vans, 89.4% of them diesel, and in 2025 MOT tests across BR postcodes the Ford Transit and Ford Transit Custom were the two most tested diesel vans. For a van carrying a load, a remap's extra torque helps, within gearbox and clutch limits. In the 2021 Census, only 22.9% of households in the council area had no car, close to the England and Wales figure of 23.3%, though just 27.9% of working residents drove to work. The nearest service area is RoadChef Clacket Lane on the M25, about 12 km away. The London ULEZ covers every borough and can charge cars and vans, and since a remap doesn't change the emissions standard, the charge is unaffected.

name: Cambridge
intro: In Cambridge, the car was not how most people got to work. In the 2021 Census, just 19.8% of working residents in the Cambridge built-up area drove to work, against 45.1% across England and Wales, and 33.9% of households had no car. Trips out of the city are where performance counts: Cambourne is 14.1 km away, Newmarket 19.1 km, and the M11 is among the main roads. That is where a Stage 1 remap shows. On a diesel, stronger mid-range torque makes overtaking and joining faster roads easier, from a change to the engine's software settings made within its limits.
driving: Other main roads include the A14, A10 and A428, and the nearest listed service areas are Four Went Ways on the A11, 10.5 km away, and Cambridge Services on the A14 at 12.3 km. In the 2021 Census, 19.3% of households in the built-up area had two or more cars. Of the 40,356 privately kept cars in the Cambridge council area at the end of June 2026, 26.5% were diesel and 57.6% petrol, and private diesel cars fell from 11,391 to 10,702 over the year. Across CB postcodes in 2025 MOT tests, the Volkswagen Golf was the most tested diesel car and the Ford Transit led the diesel vans, ahead of the Volkswagen Transporter. A loaded van benefits from extra torque, though the gearbox and clutch set the limits.

name: Camden
intro: Just 12.3% of privately kept cars in the Camden council area ran on diesel at the end of June 2026, the 4th lowest share of the 104 large towns we cover. That is 4,217 diesel cars, down from 4,442 a year earlier, while petrol made up 64.2%. For the owners of those diesels, Stage 1 remapping brings more mid-range torque, the pull that makes joining faster roads and overtaking easier. It comes from software changes to fuel, boost and timing, kept within the engine's limits, with nothing bolted on. A car with a DPF or injector fault is repaired before it is remapped.
driving: Camden sits inside the London Ultra Low Emission Zone, which covers all London boroughs and can charge cars and vans a daily fee. A remap doesn't change a vehicle's emissions standard, so it won't change whether the ULEZ charges yours. In the 2021 Census, just 6.9% of working residents in the council area drove to work, and 63.6% of households had no car. Plug-in cars made up 12.8% of private cars in June 2026, the 2nd highest share of the 104 towns. The M1 is on the main road list, and London Gateway Services on the M1 is 11.8 km away. In 2025 MOT tests across NW postcodes, the Mercedes-Benz E Class was the most tested diesel car and the Ford Transit the most tested van.

name: Cardiff
intro: With the M4, A470 and A48 among its main roads, the Welsh capital mixes city driving with quick motorway access: Cardiff Gate Services is 6 km away and Cardiff West 8.3 km. Stage 1 remapping suits that mix. In town, a diesel pulls more cleanly from low revs. On the M4 or the A470, a slip-road join or an overtake feels less strained thanks to the extra mid-range torque, and you stay in a higher gear for longer. The engine's fuel, boost and timing settings are adjusted in software, within the engine's limits. Nothing is bolted on, and the vehicle keeps the emissions standard it had before.
driving: In the 2021 Census, 39.9% of working residents in the Cardiff built-up area drove to work, below the England and Wales figure of 45.1%, and 26.5% of households had no car. Neighbouring towns are close: Penarth is 6.4 km away, Caerphilly 9 km and Barry 11.4 km. In the Cardiff council area, 29.1% of privately kept cars were diesel at the end of June 2026, and so were 96.3% of the 9,789 private vans. In 2025 MOT tests across CF postcodes, the Volkswagen Golf, Ford Focus and Nissan Qashqai were the most tested diesel cars, while the Ford Transit and Volkswagen Transporter led the vans. For a Golf or Focus, Stage 1 is about easier everyday pull. For a Transit, it is about carrying weight, within the gearbox's limits.

name: Chelmsford
intro: In the 2021 Census, 6.8% of working residents in the Chelmsford built-up area travelled 30 km or more to work, measured in a straight line, compared with 4.4% across England and Wales. Longer trips put a car's mid-range to work, and that is the part of the engine's response Stage 1 remapping improves most on a diesel. You notice it when joining a fast road, overtaking, or climbing without changing down, and no extra hardware is involved. Any fuel saving depends on how you drive and tends to be modest, so treat it as a side effect rather than the reason. A car with a warning light showing is repaired before any remap.
driving: Privately kept diesel cars in the Chelmsford council area fell from 24,537 to 22,890 in the year to June 2026, a drop of 6.7%, leaving diesel at 24% of 95,241 cars. Vans are common: 6,563 are privately kept, 69 for every 1,000 private cars, and 93.1% of them are diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across CM postcodes, the Ford Transit was the most tested diesel van and the Ford Kuga the most tested diesel car, with the Land Rover Discovery second. The A12, A130 and A414 are among the main roads, and Boreham Services on the A131 is only about 3 km away. For towing or loaded work, the torque gain is the useful part, within the limits of the gearbox and clutch.

name: Cheltenham
intro: Volkswagen Transporters ran Ford Transits close in 2025 MOT tests across GL postcodes: 6,066 diesel Transporters against 6,606 diesel Transits, the two most tested diesel vans in the area. That is a postcode area figure rather than Cheltenham's own, but vans matter in the town too. The Cheltenham council area had 3,985 privately kept vans at the end of June 2026, 70 for every 1,000 private cars, and 94.2% of them were diesel. Torque is what a Stage 1 remap adds that a van driver feels: a loaded Transporter or Transit pulls from lower revs and holds a gear for longer. Clutch and gearbox limits still apply.
driving: The M5, A40, A46 and A417 are among Cheltenham's main roads, and Gloucester Services on the M5 is 13 km away, with Strensham on the same motorway at 19 km. Bishop's Cleeve is 5.7 km from town, Gloucester 10.7 km and Tewkesbury 11.3 km. In the 2021 Census, 38.9% of working residents in the Cheltenham built-up area drove to work and 34.2% of households had two or more cars. Private diesel cars in the council area fell 7.1% in the year to June 2026, from 16,274 to 15,116, one of the steepest drops among the 104 large towns we cover, yet diesel is still 26.6% of private cars. For a diesel on the M5, extra mid-range torque makes joining and overtaking easier.

name: City of Westminster
intro: Of the 104 large towns we cover, the City of Westminster has the highest share of plug-in cars: 13.6% of privately kept cars in the Westminster council area at the end of June 2026. Diesel made up 15.7%, or 5,885 cars, and petrol 61.1%. That puts Stage 1 remapping in perspective here. It applies to the petrol and diesel cars that still make up most of the fleet, and it is software only: fuel, boost and timing, adjusted within the engine's limits. On a diesel, the difference shows as mid-range torque when pulling into faster traffic. Any fuel economy change is modest and depends on how the car is driven.
driving: Much of the West End lies inside the borough, and the main roads listed include the A4, A40, A41 and A5. The whole borough is inside the London Ultra Low Emission Zone, which can charge cars and vans daily, and a remap doesn't change a vehicle's emissions standard, so it won't change whether the charge applies. In the 2021 Census, 6.6% of working residents in the council area drove to work and 66.2% of households had no car. There were 1,052 private vans, 28 for every 1,000 cars, the 3rd lowest ratio of the 104 towns. In 2025 MOT tests across W postcodes, the Mercedes-Benz E Class led the diesel cars and the Ford Transit the vans.

name: Colchester
intro: Long commutes stand out in Colchester's 2021 Census figures. In the Colchester built-up area, 7.3% of working residents travelled 30 km or more to work, measured in a straight line, against 4.4% across England and Wales. The A12 and A120 are among the main roads. Stage 1 remapping gives a diesel more mid-range torque, which on roads like these means passing slower traffic or merging without dropping a gear. The remap itself is a software change to the engine's fuel, boost and timing settings, within its limits. Any change in fuel use depends on how you drive and is modest.
driving: The Colchester council area had 78 privately kept vans for every 1,000 private cars at the end of June 2026, the 15th highest ratio of the 104 large towns we cover, with 93.9% of the 7,417 vans on diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across CO postcodes, the Ford Transit led the diesel vans, and the Ford Kuga, not the Volkswagen Golf, was the most tested diesel car. Ardleigh South Services on the A120 is 5.1 km out, but the next nearest service area is 23.7 km away, and Halstead, Clacton-on-Sea and Sudbury are all over 19 km off. Of the council area's 94,843 private cars, 29.2% are diesel. For a loaded van or a Kuga with a trailer, Stage 1 adds pull where it is needed.

name: Coventry
intro: Coventry is still a combustion-engine city. Only 3.6% of privately kept cars in the council area were plug-ins at the end of June 2026, one of the lowest shares of the 104 large towns we cover, while petrol made up 56.1% and diesel 32.5%. With so many engines burning fuel, Stage 1 remapping stays relevant to a large number of owners. Nothing is bolted on: the remap adjusts fuel, boost and timing in the engine software and keeps within the engine's limits. On a diesel the gain sits in the mid-range, so overtaking and joining fast roads take less effort. Fuel use may change a little depending on driving style, but no saving is promised.
driving: In the 2021 Census, 46.7% of working residents in the Coventry built-up area drove to work, close to the England and Wales figure of 45.1%, and 27.7% of households had no car. Corley Services on the M6 is about 7 km from the city, and the A45, A46 and A444 are among the main roads. The council area has 8,370 privately kept vans, 95.8% diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across CV postcodes, the Ford Transit was the most tested diesel van with the Volkswagen Transporter second, and the Volkswagen Golf led the diesel cars. On a Golf, a remap means easier pace on the M6. On a loaded van it means more torque, within gearbox and clutch limits.

name: Crawley
intro: Moto Pease Pottage Services sits 3.8 km from Crawley on the M23, and Handcross on the A23 is 6.8 km away. Faster roads start close to home here, and they are where a diesel's mid-range matters: joining the M23, overtaking, holding speed without changing down. A Stage 1 remap works on exactly that part of the rev range. It is a software change to the engine's fuel, boost and timing settings, kept within the engine's limits, with nothing added to the car. At the end of June 2026, 27.1% of the 53,996 privately kept cars in the Crawley council area were diesel, more than one in four.
driving: In the 2021 Census, 47.3% of working residents in the Crawley built-up area drove to work and 5.8% travelled 30 km or more, both above the England and Wales figures of 45.1% and 4.4%. Households with two or more cars made up 37.4%. The A264 and A217 are also among Crawley's main roads, Horley is 6.6 km away and Horsham 11.1 km. The council area has 3,215 privately kept vans, 95.7% of them diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across RH postcodes, the Ford Transit was the most tested diesel van, with the Volkswagen Caddy in the top five, while the Volkswagen Golf led the diesel cars. For van drivers, the torque gain is most useful with a full load, and the clutch and gearbox decide how far it should go.

name: Croydon
intro: Mercedes-Benz and Land Rover took all five top places among diesel cars in 2025 MOT tests across CR postcodes: the E Class, C Class, Discovery, A Class and Range Rover Evoque. The CR figures cover the whole postcode area, not Croydon alone, but they show the kind of diesel that is common in this part of London. On cars like these, Stage 1 remapping shows up as mid-range torque: easier overtaking, a steadier pull with a trailer and fewer downshifts on hills. The remap adjusts fuel, boost and timing settings within the engine's limits, and nothing is bolted on. Insurers must be told about it.
driving: Croydon is an Outer London borough inside the Ultra Low Emission Zone, which can charge cars and vans daily. A remap doesn't change a vehicle's emissions standard, so the ULEZ position stays the same. The A23, A22 and A232 head the main road list, Caterham is 7 km away, and RoadChef Clacket Lane Services on the M25 is 12.2 km off. In the 2021 Census, 27.7% of working residents in the council area drove to work and 16.8% travelled 10 km or more. At the end of June 2026 the council area had 130,114 privately kept cars, 69.1% petrol and 12.6% diesel, one of the lowest diesel shares of the 104 towns. With petrol that common, a Stage 1 enquiry here may well be about a petrol car.

name: Derby
intro: Derby ranks 12th of the 104 large towns we cover for the share of private cars running on diesel. At the end of June 2026, 34.3% of privately kept cars in the Derby council area were diesel, 38,511 in all, down from 40,349 a year earlier. Stage 1 remapping on one of those cars starts with making sure nothing is wrong: a diesel with a DPF, EGR or injector fault is repaired first. After that it is a software change to the engine's fuel, boost and timing settings, kept within its limits, with nothing bolted on. The result is more mid-range torque, felt as firmer pull on hills and fewer downshifts with a load on board.
driving: Driving to work was common in Derby in the 2021 Census: 50.2% of working residents in the built-up area drove, against 45.1% across England and Wales, and 18.5% travelled 10 km or more. The A38, A50 and A52 are among the main roads, with the A6, A61 and A516, and the two closest service areas are both on the A50, Derby South at 8.2 km and Derby with Burton at 8.4 km. In 2025 MOT tests across DE postcodes, the Volkswagen Golf and Ford Focus were the most tested diesel cars, and the Ford Transit led the vans, ahead of the Volkswagen Transporter and Vauxhall Vivaro. The council area had 7,088 private vans, 95.6% of them diesel. On A-road commutes, a remap's extra torque mainly means fewer gear changes.

name: Dundee

caz.name: Dundee Low Emission Zone
caz.scope: It covers the area inside the A991 Inner Ring Road and issues penalty charges to vehicles that do not meet its standards.

intro: Inside the A991 Inner Ring Road, Dundee's Low Emission Zone applies to both cars and vans. It works by penalty charge, with no option to pay to enter, and the Bell Street, West Marketgait NCP and Wellgate car parks are left out. If you are thinking about Stage 1 remapping on a diesel, the zone is not affected either way: a remap doesn't change a vehicle's emissions standard, so it can't change whether a vehicle is charged. What changes is how the engine pulls. The remap works on fuel, boost and timing within the engine's limits, and the result is more mid-range torque for overtaking and hills.
driving: Privately kept diesel cars in the Dundee City council area fell from 14,571 to 13,251 in the year to June 2026, a drop of 9.1% and one of the steepest of the 104 large towns we cover. Diesel is still 23.7% of private cars, and there are 3,173 privately kept vans, 97.1% of them diesel. The A90 is on the main road list, with Forfar Services on the A90 about 18 km away. In 2025 MOT tests across DD postcodes, the Ford Transit was the most tested diesel van by a wide margin, and the Volkswagen Golf led the diesel cars. For those keeping a diesel, a remap adds pull on the A90, and a loaded van gains torque within its gearbox and clutch limits.

name: Ealing
intro: The M4 and the A40 both appear among Ealing's main roads, and Moto Heston Services on the M4 is just 5 km away. Yet the car on an Ealing driveway is far more often petrol than diesel: 65.8% of the 105,587 privately kept cars in the council area ran on petrol at the end of June 2026, against 15.1% on diesel. A Stage 1 remap is not only for diesels: on a petrol car, the same kind of engine settings are adjusted in software, within the engine's limits. On a diesel, the gain most drivers notice is mid-range torque, the pull you use when joining the M4 or overtaking.
driving: Other main roads include the A406 and A312, and Hounslow is 6.5 km away. In the 2021 Census, 24.5% of working residents in the Ealing council area drove to work, against 45.1% across England and Wales, and 36.8% of households had no car. Vans are relatively few in the council area: 4,219, or 40 for every 1,000 private cars, one of the lowest ratios of the 104. In 2025 MOT tests across W postcodes, the Mercedes-Benz E Class was the most tested diesel car and the Ford Transit the most tested diesel van. Ealing sits within the ULEZ like every London borough. Its daily charge can apply to cars and vans, and because a remap leaves the emissions standard alone, it makes no difference to whether you pay.

name: Edinburgh

caz.name: Edinburgh Low Emission Zone
caz.scope: It covers the city centre and issues penalty charges to vehicles that do not meet its standards.

intro: Private diesel cars in the City of Edinburgh council area fell from 38,167 to 34,481 in the year to June 2026, a drop of 9.7% and the 2nd biggest fall of the 104 large towns we cover. Diesel now makes up 19.9% of the 173,168 privately kept cars there. For drivers who are keeping a diesel, Stage 1 remapping is a way to change how it drives without changing the car. The remap is a software change to fuel, boost and timing, within the engine's limits, and the gain you notice is mid-range torque. A car with a DPF, AdBlue, EGR or injector fault is repaired before any remap.
driving: The Edinburgh Low Emission Zone covers the city centre, including Tollcross, Queen Street, Picardy Place, Abbeyhill and the Meadows. It applies to cars and vans through penalty charges, with no option to pay to enter. A remap doesn't change a vehicle's emissions standard, so it doesn't change how the zone treats yours. Away from the centre, the A720 and A8 are on the main road list, Dreghorn Services on the A720 is 4.8 km away, and Moto Musselburgh Services on the A1 is 9.5 km. The council area had 9,239 private vans in June 2026, 93.8% diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across EH postcodes, the Ford Transit led the diesel vans and the Volkswagen Golf the cars, with the Land Rover Discovery second.

name: Enfield
intro: Diesel cars are holding their ground in Enfield. The council area had 17,803 privately kept diesel cars at the end of June 2026, against 18,258 a year earlier, a fall of 2.5% that is the 5th smallest of the 104 large towns we cover. Diesel is still a minority, at 16.3% of private cars against 67.4% on petrol. For those who hold on to one, the case for Stage 1 remapping rests on mid-range torque: on the A10 and A406 a remapped diesel pulls from low revs without hunting for a lower gear. Nothing is bolted on. The fuel, boost and timing settings are changed in software, within the engine's limits.
driving: London's ULEZ covers all London boroughs, Enfield included, though not the M25 itself, and it charges cars and vans daily. A remap does not change an engine's emissions standard, so it cannot change whether a vehicle pays. The M25, A10, A406 and A110 are among the borough's main roads, and South Mimms Services on the A1(M) is 10 km away. In the 2021 Census, 18.5% of working residents in the Enfield council area travelled 10 km or more to work, and 32.5% drove. In 2025 MOT tests across EN postcodes, the Mercedes-Benz E Class and C Class were the most tested diesel cars, and the Ford Transit led the diesel vans. For a large diesel saloon on the M25, Stage 1 mostly means easier overtaking.

name: Gateshead

caz.name: Newcastle and Gateshead (Tyneside) Clean Air Zone
caz.scope: It covers part of central Newcastle and Gateshead, including the Tyne crossings, and charges vans, not private cars.

intro: Motorway-status roads make up three of the eight on Gateshead's main road list: the A1(M), A194(M) and A167(M). Moto Washington Services, on the A1(M), is about 6 km away. Roads like these call for clean joins at speed, and the extra mid-range torque from Stage 1 remapping helps a diesel get up to pace without hunting for a lower gear. The work is done in the engine software, where fuel, boost and timing are adjusted within the engine's limits, and nothing is bolted on. Any change in fuel use is modest and depends on how you drive. If the car has a DPF or EGR fault, that is repaired first.
driving: The Newcastle and Gateshead (Tyneside) Clean Air Zone covers part of both, including the central area and the Tyne crossings. It can charge vans but does not charge private cars, and since a remap doesn't change a vehicle's emissions standard, it won't change whether a van is charged. The Gateshead council area has 5,565 privately kept vans, 71 for every 1,000 private cars, 96.1% of them diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across NE postcodes, the Ford Transit was the most tested diesel van and the Volkswagen Golf the most tested diesel car. In the 2021 Census, 37.8% of households in the Gateshead built-up area had no car, against 23.3% across England and Wales. For a working van, extra torque under load is the point, within gearbox and clutch limits.

name: Gillingham
intro: Commuting distances in Gillingham stood out in the 2021 Census. In the Gillingham built-up area, 7.9% of working residents travelled 30 km or more to work, measured in a straight line, against 4.4% across England and Wales, and 20.9% travelled 10 km or more. Census day fell in a lockdown, when commuting was lower than usual. On longer runs, a Stage 1 remap is about the mid-range. A diesel that pulls more strongly from lower revs overtakes more easily and changes down less often. The change is made in software and stays within the engine's limits, with no extra parts fitted.
driving: Gillingham runs into Chatham, Rochester, Strood and Rainham as one built-up area, and Chatham is just 3.4 km away. Moto Medway Services on the M2 is 2.9 km out, with Maidstone Services on the M20 at 11 km. In the 2021 Census, 49.4% of working residents drove to work and 38.4% of households had two or more cars. The Medway council area had 134,818 privately kept cars at the end of June 2026, 27.7% of them diesel, plus 9,337 private vans, 94.9% diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across ME postcodes, the Ford Transit was the most tested diesel van and the Volkswagen Golf the most tested diesel car. Vans like these gain the most usable pull when loaded, as long as the clutch and gearbox can take it.

name: Glasgow

caz.name: Glasgow Low Emission Zone
caz.scope: It covers about one square mile of the city centre and issues penalty charges to vehicles that do not meet its standards.

intro: Glasgow's Low Emission Zone covers about one square mile of the city centre and applies to cars and vans, with penalty charges rather than a fee to enter. If you are weighing up Stage 1 remapping, the key point is this: a remap doesn't change a vehicle's emissions standard, so it won't change whether the zone applies to yours. What it does change is how the engine delivers its power. On a diesel, the gain is mid-range torque, which helps when joining motorway traffic or overtaking. Nothing is bolted on; the remap adjusts fuel, boost and timing within the engine's limits.
driving: The M8, M74, M77 and M80 are all on the main road list, and RoadChef Bothwell Services on the M74 is 13.6 km away. Rutherglen is 5.6 km off and Bishopbriggs 6.3 km. The Glasgow City council area had 200,595 privately kept cars at the end of June 2026, 63.2% petrol and 24.5% diesel. Private diesel cars fell from 53,884 to 49,062 over the year, a drop of 8.9% and the 4th biggest of the 104 large towns we cover. There were 10,839 private vans, 96.5% diesel, and in 2025 MOT tests across G postcodes the Ford Transit was the most tested diesel van, with 9,359. On a van, the clutch and gearbox set the limit on how much extra torque Stage 1 should add.

name: Gloucester
intro: Eighty privately kept vans for every 1,000 private cars: that was the ratio in the Gloucester council area at the end of June 2026, the 12th highest of the 104 large towns we cover. Of those 5,170 vans, 95.9% ran on diesel. For a van owner, what counts is how the engine copes with weight on board, and that is the part Stage 1 remapping improves. Adjusting the fuel, boost and timing settings within the engine's limits gives more mid-range torque, so a loaded van pulls away more easily and holds a higher gear. The gearbox and clutch still set the limits, and a remap file matched to the vehicle has to respect them.
driving: The M5 is among Gloucester's main roads, with the A38, A40, A417 and A48, and Westmorland Gloucester Services on the M5 is just 4 km away. In the 2021 Census, 51.4% of working residents in the Gloucester built-up area drove to work, above the England and Wales figure of 45.1%, and 37% of households had two or more cars. Churchdown, Brockworth and Quedgeley and Hardwicke are all within 5.5 km, and Cheltenham is 10.7 km. In 2025 MOT tests across GL postcodes, the Ford Transit and Volkswagen Transporter were close for most tested diesel van, 6,606 against 6,066, and the Volkswagen Golf led the cars. Diesel made up 31.8% of private cars in the council area. On the M5, a remap's torque makes joining and overtaking easier.

name: Greenwich
intro: Mercedes-Benz took the top three places among diesel cars given an MOT across SE postcodes in 2025: the E Class, the C Class and the A Class, followed by the BMW 5 Series and 3 Series. The SE area reaches well beyond Greenwich, but the list shows the kind of diesel that is common in this part of London: premium saloons and hatchbacks. On cars like these, Stage 1 remapping is about a smoother, stronger mid-range rather than outright pace. A heavier saloon like an E Class feels it most when joining a fast road or overtaking, where the extra torque means fewer downshifts. The car keeps its standard hardware, and your insurer must be told about the change.
driving: In the 2021 Census, 43.1% of households in the Greenwich council area had no car, against 23.3% across England and Wales, and only 20% of working residents drove to work. Diesel is a small part of the car mix: 14.2% of the 71,604 privately kept cars at the end of June 2026, with petrol at 68.8%. The A102, A205 and A2213 are among the main roads, and the nearest service area is Moto Thurrock on the M25, about 16 km away. The council area has 2,919 privately kept vans, 90.6% diesel, and the Ford Transit led the diesel vans in the SE MOT figures. The ULEZ covers all London boroughs and can charge cars and vans. A remap doesn't change a vehicle's emissions standard, so it won't change that.

name: Hackney
intro: Most households in the Hackney council area had no car at all in the 2021 Census: 64.9%, against 23.3% across England and Wales. Only 8.7% of working residents drove to work. So if you do keep a car or van in Hackney, it pays to think about how you really use it before deciding on a Stage 1 remap. The gain is mid-range torque, which you feel most with a loaded van or on a faster road out of London, and much less in stop-start traffic. On a van, the gearbox and clutch set how far the remap should go, and nothing physical is added to the engine.
driving: None of the main roads listed for Hackney is a motorway: they include the A10, A12, A102 and A1. The nearest listed service area is London Gateway on the M1, 16.6 km away. Islington is 2.7 km from Hackney and Tower Hamlets 4.1 km. At the end of June 2026 the council area had 36,788 privately kept cars, 67.6% petrol and 14.1% diesel, and 1,734 private vans, 85.8% of them diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across E postcodes, the Ford Transit was the most tested diesel van, followed by the Mercedes-Benz Sprinter and Vito. Cars and vans can both face the ULEZ daily charge here. A remap does not move a vehicle into or out of it, because the emissions standard stays the same.

name: Hammersmith and Fulham
intro: Inside Hammersmith and Fulham, as in every London borough, the Ultra Low Emission Zone can apply a daily charge to cars and vans. Plug-in cars already made up 10.1% of privately kept cars in the council area at the end of June 2026, the 4th highest share of the 104 large towns we cover, though petrol, at 66%, is still the main fuel. For those petrol and diesel cars, Stage 1 remapping changes fuel, boost and timing settings within the engine's limits, giving more mid-range torque for pulling into faster traffic. It doesn't change the emissions standard, so a car's ULEZ position stays exactly as it was.
driving: The A4 Great West Road and the A40 Westway both run east to west through the borough, and the M4 is on the main road list, with Moto Heston Services on the M4 11.6 km away. In the 2021 Census, 7.9% of working residents in the council area drove to work and 57.5% of households had no car. Diesel made up 14.8% of the 37,547 privately kept cars at the end of June 2026, and private diesel cars fell from 5,925 to 5,572 over the year. In 2025 MOT tests across W postcodes, the Land Rover Discovery was the second most tested diesel car, behind the Mercedes-Benz E Class. For a car heading out along the A4 or M4, Stage 1 makes joining and overtaking easier.

name: Haringey
intro: More than half of Haringey households had no car in the 2021 Census: 52.7% across the council area, against 23.3% for England and Wales, and only 13.7% of working residents drove to work. Diesel is a small share of what is kept, too. At the end of June 2026, 13.9% of privately kept cars in the Haringey council area were diesel, one of the lowest shares of the 104 large towns we cover, with petrol on 68.6%. Stage 1 remapping applies to turbocharged petrol engines as well as diesels: it is a software change to the fuel, boost and timing settings, kept within the engine's limits. In town traffic the benefit is smoother pull at low revs rather than outright speed.
driving: The borough runs from high ground around Highgate and Muswell Hill down to flat land by the River Lea, so a local round can include steep climbs. That is where a diesel van's extra mid-range torque shows: fewer downshifts and less strain with a load on board. Haringey's council area had 2,477 privately kept vans at the end of June 2026, 89% of them diesel. London's ULEZ covers the whole borough and charges cars and vans daily, and a remap does not change whether a vehicle pays. The A1, A10, A406 and A503 are among the main roads. In 2025 MOT tests across N postcodes, the Ford Transit and Mercedes-Benz Sprinter led the diesel vans, and the Mercedes-Benz E Class led the cars.

name: Harrow
intro: Vans are thin on the ground in the Harrow council area: 32 privately kept vans for every 1,000 private cars, one of the lowest ratios of the 104 large towns we cover. So remapping here is mostly a question about cars, and petrol leads with 62% of private cars against 14.4% for diesel. The M1 is on Harrow's main road list, and London Gateway Services on it is about 7 km away. For a car that regularly heads out that way, Stage 1 remapping brings a stronger mid-range for joining at speed and passing slower traffic. On either fuel it is a software job on fuel, boost and timing, inside the engine's limits, with no hardware added.
driving: In the 2021 Census, 30.3% of working residents in the council area drove to work, below the England and Wales figure of 45.1%, and 31% of households had two or more cars. Plug-ins make up 8.1% of private cars, one of the highest shares of the 104, and petrol hybrids 15.1%. The A312 and A4090 are among the main roads. In 2025 MOT tests across HA postcodes, the Mercedes-Benz E Class was the most tested diesel car, ahead of the C Class and the BMW 5 Series. On a large diesel saloon, a remap is mostly about relaxed, stronger pull. The London ULEZ covers the borough and can charge cars and vans, and a remap doesn't alter the emissions standard that decides it.

name: Havering
intro: Every London borough sits inside the Ultra Low Emission Zone, Havering included, and Havering is the easternmost of them. The M25, which is among Havering's main roads, is not part of the zone. If you are weighing up a Stage 1 remap here, the ULEZ point is simple: a remap does not change a vehicle's emissions standard, so it does not change whether the zone's daily charge applies to your car or van. What it does change is how the engine delivers its power. The fuel, boost and timing settings are adjusted in software, within the engine's limits, and on a diesel the gain you feel most is mid-range pull for overtaking and joining faster roads.
driving: The A127 and A12 are also among Havering's main roads, and Moto Thurrock Services on the M25 is 10.2 km away. In the 2021 Census, 21.2% of working residents in the Havering council area travelled 10 km or more to work, above the England and Wales figure of 19%, and 34.3% of households had two or more cars. Diesel makes up 16.6% of the 107,173 private cars in the council area, and the number fell just 3.3% over the year to June 2026, one of the smallest falls of the 104. The council area also has 5,782 private vans, 92.8% diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across RM postcodes, the Ford Kuga was the most tested diesel car and the Ford Transit the most tested diesel van.

name: Hillingdon
intro: With the M4, M40 and M25 all on its main road list, plus the A40 and A312, Hillingdon puts fast roads close to home. Moto Heston Services on the M4 is 6.5 km away and ExtraMSA Beaconsfield Services on the M40 is 13.9 km. For a diesel that uses those roads, Stage 1 remapping is about mid-range torque: overtaking and holding speed with a load on board, with fewer downshifts. No parts are added. The remap changes software settings and stays inside the engine's limits, and any change in fuel economy is modest and depends on how you drive.
driving: Hillingdon is inside the London Ultra Low Emission Zone, which covers all London boroughs but not the M25 itself, and can charge cars and vans daily. A remap doesn't alter a vehicle's emissions standard, so the ULEZ position stays as it was. In the 2021 Census, 38.8% of working residents in the council area drove to work and 22.3% of households had no car, slightly below the England and Wales figure of 23.3%. At the end of June 2026 there were 119,789 privately kept cars, 66.9% petrol and 15.5% diesel, and private diesel cars fell by only 3.7% over the year. The 5,814 private vans were 92.7% diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across UB postcodes, the Ford Transit and Mercedes-Benz Sprinter led the diesel vans.

name: Hounslow
intro: Moto Heston Services sits on the M4 just 2.5 km from Hounslow, and the M3 is also on the borough's list of main roads, alongside the A4, A30, A312 and A316. With two motorways on that list, plenty of journeys can include a slip road and a stretch of fast traffic. That is where Stage 1 remapping is easiest to feel: on a diesel, extra mid-range torque brings the car up to speed with less effort and makes overtaking less of a stretch. The change is made in software, to the fuel, boost and timing settings, within the engine's limits. Fuel use changes are modest and depend on how you drive.
driving: In the 2021 Census, 29.4% of working residents in the Hounslow council area drove to work and 14.5% travelled 10 km or more, while 32.8% of households had no car. Petrol leads the private fleet: 66.4% of privately kept cars in the council area at the end of June 2026, with petrol hybrids on 11% and diesel on 15.2%. In 2025 MOT tests across TW postcodes, the Mercedes-Benz E Class and C Class were the most tested diesel cars, and the Ford Transit and Mercedes-Benz Sprinter led the vans. London's ULEZ covers the borough and charges cars and vans, and a remap leaves the emissions standard unchanged, so the charge is unaffected. Richmond upon Thames is 4.4 km away and Ealing 6.5 km.

name: Huddersfield
intro: With 14,637 privately kept vans at the end of June 2026, the Kirklees council area, which covers Huddersfield, has 74 vans for every 1,000 private cars, and 95.2% of them run on diesel. A working diesel van needs to be healthy before any Stage 1 remapping: an AdBlue, DPF or EGR fault is repaired first, because a remap is not a fix for a fault. Once the van is sound, a remap file matched to the vehicle raises mid-range torque, so a loaded van holds its gear on a hill rather than dropping down. Nothing is bolted on, and the change works within the engine's limits, with the gearbox and clutch setting how far it can go.
driving: In the 2021 Census, 49.7% of working residents in the Huddersfield built-up area drove to work, above the England and Wales figure of 45.1%, and 29.6% of households had no car. Welcome Break Hartshead Moor on the M62 is about 8 km away, and the A616, A641 and A644 are among the main roads. Diesel makes up 31.9% of private cars in Kirklees, and their number fell 5.3% over the year to June 2026. In 2025 MOT tests across HD postcodes, the Volkswagen Golf was the most tested diesel car, with about twice as many as the Audi A3, and the Ford Transit led the diesel vans. On a diesel Golf, a remap gives stronger pull on climbs and easier motorway joins.

name: Ipswich
intro: At 35.2%, the diesel share of privately kept cars in the Ipswich council area is the joint 10th highest among the 104 large towns we cover, while plug-ins make up just 3.1%, one of the lowest shares (end of June 2026). If you drive one of those diesels, a Stage 1 remap is worth understanding before you decide. It changes how the engine is set up, not what is fitted to it, and the result is stronger pulling in the middle of the rev range, where you overtake and climb. A diesel with an injector, EGR or DPF fault needs that put right first.
driving: A service area on the A14 is 2.6 km away, and the A12 is also among Ipswich's main roads. Kesgrave is 6.2 km away. In the 2021 Census, 48.3% of working residents in the Ipswich built-up area drove to work and 5% travelled 30 km or more, both above the England and Wales figures of 45.1% and 4.4%. Private diesel cars in the council area fell only from 22,795 to 22,046 over the year, one of the smallest falls of the 104. The council area has 4,491 private vans, 94.8% diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across IP postcodes, the Ford Transit led the diesel vans and the Ford Ranger made the top five. For towing or a full load, extra torque is the point, within gearbox and clutch limits.

name: Islington
intro: Fewer than one working resident in ten drove to work in the Islington council area in the 2021 Census: 6.8%, against 45.1% across England and Wales. Only 0.9% travelled 30 km or more. Census day fell in a lockdown, so these figures were lower than usual, but they point to short, urban driving. That shapes what Stage 1 remapping does for the cars that are kept here. The gain is mid-range torque, felt when pulling away, merging into faster traffic or climbing, rather than at sustained high speed. It is a software change to fuel, boost and timing settings, within the engine's limits, with nothing bolted on.
driving: Islington's listed main roads are all A roads, including the A1, A10, A104 and A501, and the nearest listed service area, London Gateway Services on the M1, is 14.9 km away. The whole borough is inside the London Ultra Low Emission Zone, which can charge cars and vans daily, and a remap doesn't change a vehicle's emissions standard. In the 2021 Census, 66.9% of households in the council area had no car. Of the 29,457 privately kept cars at the end of June 2026, 68.3% were petrol and 12.6% diesel, while plug-ins made up 9.1%, the 6th highest share of the 104 towns. In 2025 MOT tests across N postcodes, the Mercedes-Benz E Class led the diesel cars and the Ford Transit the vans.

name: Kensington and Chelsea
intro: Plug-in cars make up 12.7% of privately kept cars in the Kensington and Chelsea council area, the 3rd highest share of the 104 large towns we cover. Diesel is down to 15%, and petrol accounts for 63.7%. Most private cars here still have a combustion engine, and that is what Stage 1 remapping works on: a software change to the fuel, boost and timing settings of a petrol or diesel engine, kept within its limits. Nothing is bolted on. A diesel gains most in the mid-range, so pulling away and overtaking take less effort. Your insurer must be told about any remap.
driving: Most households here have no car. In the 2021 Census, 58.3% of households in the Kensington and Chelsea council area were without one, and just 7.7% of working residents drove to work. Vans are scarce too: 27 privately kept vans per 1,000 private cars, the second lowest ratio of the 104 large towns we cover, and only 78.3% of those 943 vans were diesel. London's ULEZ covers the borough and charges both cars and vans, and a remap does not change a vehicle's emissions standard. In 2025 MOT tests across SW postcodes, the Land Rover Discovery was the most tested diesel car, ahead of the Mercedes-Benz E Class and Range Rover Evoque. For a heavy SUV like the Discovery, Stage 1 brings easier pull at low revs.

name: Kingston upon Hull
intro: Hull leans on diesel more than most of the 104 large towns we cover. In the Kingston upon Hull council area, 36.4% of privately kept cars were diesel at the end of June 2026, one of the highest shares, while plug-ins were just 3.2%, one of the lowest. The diesel count fell by 3.1% over the year, a smaller drop than most. That makes the diesel the obvious candidate for Stage 1 remapping here, and the effect is easy to describe: more torque in the middle of the rev range, so the car pulls harder without needing a lower gear. Nothing is fitted; only the fuel, boost and timing settings change, within the engine's limits.
driving: Journeys here run on A roads: the A63, A1033, A165 and A1079 are among the main roads, and the nearest service area is Ulceby Truckstop on the A160, about 16 km away. In the 2021 Census, 52.1% of working residents in the Kingston upon Hull built-up area drove to work, above the England and Wales figure of 45.1%, and 34.7% of households had no car. The council area has 7,101 privately kept vans, 96.9% of them diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across HU postcodes, the Nissan Qashqai was the most tested diesel car and the Ford Transit the most tested diesel van. On A road runs, stronger mid-range pull makes a Qashqai or a Transit easier to drive, within the van's gearbox and clutch limits.

name: Kingston upon Thames
intro: Near the bottom of the 104 large towns we cover for diesel, and near the top for plug-ins: that is where the Kingston upon Thames council area sits. Diesel makes up 12.7% of its 61,111 privately kept cars, one of the lowest shares, while plug-ins account for 8%, the joint 14th highest. Private diesel cars also fell from 8,340 to 7,768 in the year to June 2026, one of the steepest drops in the group. That leaves a smaller set of drivers for whom a Stage 1 remap is relevant: those keeping a diesel or petrol car. For them, the change is in software only, within the engine's limits, and it has to be declared to the insurer.
driving: Every main road listed for Kingston is an A-road, including the A3, A240, A308 and A24. The nearest listed service areas are Moto Heston on the M4 at 13 km and Cobham on the M25 at 13.4 km. In the 2021 Census, 25.1% of working residents in the council area drove to work, against 45.1% across England and Wales, and 25.7% of households had no car. Petrol makes up 68% of private cars in the council area. In 2025 MOT tests across KT postcodes, the Mercedes-Benz E Class led the diesel cars and the Ford Transit the diesel vans. The ULEZ daily charge can apply to cars and vans in the borough, and a remap cannot change whether it does, since the emissions standard stays the same.

name: Kingswood and Fishponds
intro: Many homes in Kingswood and Fishponds run more than one car. In the 2021 Census, 41.6% of households in the built-up area had two or more cars, against 35.4% across England and Wales, and only 15.8% had none. When there is more than one car on the drive, it usually makes sense to look at Stage 1 remapping for the one that works hardest: the vehicle that tows, carries a load or does the longer runs. On a diesel, new fuel, boost and timing settings add mid-range torque, within the engine's limits, so it pulls with less effort and needs fewer downshifts.
driving: The A4174 ring road runs along the eastern edge of Kingswood, and the M4, M32 and A4 are on the main road list. Avon Lodge on the A4 is 13.4 km away and Welcome Break Gordano Services on the M5 is 14.3 km. Vans stand out in the South Gloucestershire council area: 14,634 privately kept vans at the end of June 2026, 91 for every 1,000 private cars, the 5th highest ratio of the 104 towns, and 94.3% of them diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across BS postcodes, the Ford Transit and Volkswagen Transporter led the diesel vans. In the 2021 Census, 48% of working residents in the built-up area drove to work. A loaded van gains most from Stage 1 torque, within clutch and gearbox limits.

name: Lambeth
intro: At 13%, the diesel share of privately kept cars in the Lambeth council area is one of the lowest of the 104 large towns we cover, and petrol makes up 70.5%. Stage 1 remapping works on the same principle for both fuels: a software change to the engine's fuel, boost and timing settings, within its limits, with nothing bolted on. On a diesel van, the gain is mostly mid-range torque, which helps when pulling away loaded through traffic. On a petrol car the same settings are adjusted, and any difference in fuel use depends on how you drive. A vehicle with a DPF, EGR or injector fault is repaired before it is remapped.
driving: London's geographical centre lies within the borough, at Frazier Street. Main roads include the A23, A24, A3, A205 and A214, and the nearest service area, Moto Heston on the M4, is 20 km away. In the 2021 Census, 6.7% of working residents in the Lambeth council area travelled 10 km or more to work, and 58% of households had no car. Vans are few: 39 privately kept vans per 1,000 private cars, one of the lowest ratios of the 104 large towns we cover, and 85.8% of the 2,188 vans were diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across SE postcodes, the Ford Transit and Mercedes-Benz Sprinter were the most tested diesel vans. The ULEZ covers the borough and charges cars and vans, and a remap does not change who pays.

name: Leeds
intro: There were 98,140 privately kept diesel cars in the Leeds council area at the end of June 2026, 30.3% of the 324,311 private cars there, even after a 4.8% fall over the year. If you own one of them and hope a remap will cut your fuel bills, keep expectations modest: any change in economy depends on how the car is driven. The real reason for Stage 1 remapping is drivability. More mid-range torque means easier overtaking, stronger joins onto fast roads and fewer downshifts on hills, and it comes from a remap file matched to the vehicle, not from new parts. Your insurer must be told.
driving: Vans are a large group in the Leeds council area: 21,030 are privately kept, 95.9% of them diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across LS postcodes, the Ford Transit was the most tested diesel van and the Volkswagen Golf the most tested diesel car, ahead of the Ford Focus and BMW 3 Series. In the 2021 Census, 38.4% of working residents in the Leeds built-up area drove to work, below the 45.1% for England and Wales, and 35.1% of households had no car. Skelton Lake Service Station on the M1 is about 7 km away, and Exelby Services Whitwood on the M62 about 15 km. For a working van, a remap adds torque under load, within gearbox and clutch limits.

name: Leicester
intro: Around 45,000 diesel cars are privately kept in the Leicester council area: 45,079 at the end of June 2026, or 35.4% of all private cars, the 8th highest diesel share among the 104 large towns we cover. The count has barely shifted either, down 3% on a year earlier, one of the smallest falls in that group. For the drivers of those cars, the reason to consider a Stage 1 remap is mid-range torque: the pull that gets a car past slower traffic and up to speed on a slip road without dropping a gear. Any fuel saving depends on how the car is driven, so it is never something to count on.
driving: The M1 and M69 both feature among Leicester's main roads, along with the A6 and A47, and Leicester Forest East Services on the M1 is 4.7 km away. Wigston is 5.5 km away. In the 2021 Census, 44.9% of working residents in the Leicester built-up area drove to work and 30.8% of households had no car. In the council area, plug-ins are just 3.3% of private cars, one of the lowest shares of the 104, and 96.5% of the 5,848 private vans are diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across LE postcodes, the Volkswagen Golf was the most tested diesel car and the Ford Transit the most tested diesel van. With a van, the remap is shaped around the gearbox and clutch as well as the engine.

name: Lewisham
intro: Lewisham leans heavily towards petrol. At the end of June 2026, 72.3% of privately kept cars in the council area ran on it, and diesel made up just 12.2%, the 3rd lowest diesel share of the 104 large towns we cover. So if you are looking at Stage 1 remapping in Lewisham, there is a good chance the car is a petrol. Petrol or diesel, the job is the same in principle: fuel, boost and timing settings are adjusted in software, within the engine's limits. On the 8,555 diesel cars, down from 8,956 a year earlier, the change shows most as mid-range torque. On either fuel, insurers must be told about a remap.
driving: The A2, A20, A21 and A205 head Lewisham's main road list, which has no motorway, and RoadChef Clacket Lane Services on the M25, the nearest listed service area, is 20 km away. The whole borough falls within the London Ultra Low Emission Zone, which can charge cars and vans daily, and a remap won't change a vehicle's emissions standard. In the 2021 Census, 15.9% of working residents in the council area drove to work and 47.7% of households had no car. The 3,010 private vans were 87.3% diesel at the end of June 2026, and in 2025 MOT tests across SE postcodes the Ford Transit and Mercedes-Benz Sprinter led the diesel vans. Stage 1 suits a van that carries a load, within clutch and gearbox limits.

name: Lincoln
intro: Across LN postcodes, 46.2% of the cars and small vans given an MOT in 2025 were diesel. The council figures point the same way: at the end of June 2026, 35.2% of privately kept cars in the Lincoln council area ran on diesel, the 10th highest share of the 104 large towns we cover. For diesel owners, Stage 1 remapping changes the fuel, boost and timing settings within the engine's limits, with nothing bolted on. In practice that means mid-range torque: overtaking on A roads with less waiting for a gap, and fewer downshifts with a load. Insurers must be told about a remap, and any fault is repaired first.
driving: No motorway appears among Lincoln's main roads. The A46, A15, A57 and A607 do that job, with the A1192 and A1434, and Thorpe on the Hill Services on the A46 is 5.2 km out. North Hykeham is just 2.9 km away, but Newark-on-Trent is 21.4 km and Sleaford 25.8 km. In the 2021 Census, 5.9% of working residents in the Lincoln built-up area travelled 30 km or more to work, above the England and Wales figure of 4.4%. Plug-in cars are rare: 3.6% of private cars in the council area, one of the lowest shares of the 104. In 2025 MOT tests across LN postcodes, the Ford Transit and Vauxhall Vivaro were the most tested diesel vans. Longer A-road trips are where a remap's extra torque is most useful.

name: Liverpool
intro: Two Fords head the list of diesel cars given an MOT across L postcodes in 2025: the Focus, with 5,527, and the Kuga, with 4,482. The Nissan Qashqai, BMW 3 Series and Volkswagen Golf follow. These are mostly everyday family cars, and that shapes what Stage 1 remapping means here: a stronger, more relaxed engine for daily driving rather than a performance project. Only the software changes, with fuel, boost and timing adjusted inside the engine's limits. On a diesel Focus or Kuga, the gain shows as mid-range torque: easier overtaking, smoother joins onto fast roads and fewer downshifts with a full car. Tell your insurer once it is done.
driving: In the 2021 Census, 39.5% of households in the Liverpool built-up area had no car, well above the England and Wales figure of 23.3%, and 40.4% of working residents drove to work. Earlsfield Services on the M57 is about 7 km away, and Old Meadow Services on the M58 about 12 km. Diesel is 29.5% of the council area's 154,751 private cars, down 5.4% in the year to June 2026. There are 9,071 privately kept vans, 96.8% of them diesel, and the Ford Transit was the most tested diesel van across L postcodes in 2025, well ahead of the Mercedes-Benz Sprinter. A loaded van gains torque from a remap, within gearbox and clutch limits.

name: Luton
intro: Commercial vehicle manufacturing in Luton came to an end in 2025, but vans still matter here. The Luton council area had 4,554 privately kept vans at the end of June 2026, 96.7% of them diesel, and in 2025 MOT tests across LU postcodes the Ford Transit was the most tested diesel van, ahead of the Mercedes-Benz Sprinter. If yours is a van that spends the day loaded, the first thing you would notice after a Stage 1 remap is how it pulls from low revs, with fewer gear changes. How far the remap goes depends on the clutch and gearbox as well as the engine.
driving: The M1 is among Luton's main roads, with the A5, A6, A505 and A1081, and Toddington Services on the M1 is 7.9 km away. The next nearest listed service area, Bourne End on the A41, is 18.5 km out. Dunstable is 7.4 km from Luton. In the 2021 Census, 21.2% of working residents in the Luton built-up area travelled 10 km or more to work and 6.9% went 30 km or more, both above the England and Wales figures of 19% and 4.4%. Of the 90,284 private cars in the council area, 31.9% are diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across LU postcodes, the Volkswagen Golf was the most tested diesel car, with the Vauxhall Astra in the top five. On longer runs, mid-range torque is what you notice.

name: Maidstone
intro: Two motorways sit close to Maidstone: RoadChef Maidstone Services on the M20 is 6.5 km away, and Moto Medway Services on the M2 is 9.9 km. Joining a motorway from a slip road is the moment most drivers feel what Stage 1 remapping does on a diesel: the extra torque arrives in the mid-range, so the car gathers speed without dropping a gear. The changes are to fuel, boost and timing settings, within the engine's limits, with nothing bolted on. Any DPF, EGR or injector fault is repaired first, and fuel economy changes are modest and depend on driving style.
driving: Around Kent's county town the main road list adds the A229, A249, A20 and A26, and Larkfield is 6.1 km away.
