In the 2021 Census, 49.8% of working residents in the built-up area drove to work and 6.3% travelled 30 km or more, both above the England and Wales figures of 45.1% and 4.4%, and 40.3% of households had two or more cars. The Maidstone council area had 7,938 privately kept vans at the end of June 2026, 81 for every 1,000 private cars, the 11th highest of the 104 towns, and 93.2% were diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across ME postcodes, the Ford Kuga was the second most tested diesel car. For a loaded van, Stage 1 adds pulling power within clutch and gearbox limits.

name: Manchester
intro: Motorways feature heavily in Manchester's list of main roads: the M60, M602 and M67, plus the A57(M). Diesel, meanwhile, still made up 30.9% of privately kept cars in the Manchester council area at the end of June 2026, about 51,000 cars. Stage 1 remapping on one of those diesels changes the fuel, boost and timing settings in software, within the engine's limits, with nothing bolted on. Most of the gain is mid-range torque, so the car responds sooner when you put your foot down to merge or pass, without dropping a gear. Any change in fuel use is modest and depends on how you drive.
driving: In the 2021 Census, 40% of households in the Manchester built-up area had no car, against 23.3% across England and Wales, and 33.4% of working residents drove to work. Neighbouring places are close: Droylsden is 4.1 km away, Failsworth 4.8 km and Salford 5.2 km. The nearest service area, Moto Birch on the M62, is 10.4 km out. In 2025 MOT tests across M postcodes, the Volkswagen Golf, Nissan Qashqai and BMW 3 Series were the most tested diesel cars, and the Ford Transit and Mercedes-Benz Sprinter led the vans. The council area had 8,551 private vans, 96.1% of them diesel. In stop-start city traffic, a remap's low-rev torque means smoother pulling away, and a diesel with a DPF fault is repaired first.

name: Merton
intro: Big diesel SUVs and saloons top the 2025 MOT figures for SW postcodes. The Land Rover Discovery was the most tested diesel car, with 1,149, ahead of the Mercedes-Benz E Class and the Range Rover Evoque. The SW area covers far more than Merton, but heavy cars like these are where extra torque is easiest to feel. For a Discovery, Stage 1 remapping is mostly about the mid-range: easier towing, smoother overtaking and fewer downshifts on a hill. Nothing is bolted on, and the engine's limits are respected. Insurers must be told about it, and any existing fault, such as a DPF or EGR problem, is put right first.
driving: Diesel is a small share in the Merton council area: 12.4% of privately kept cars at the end of June 2026, one of the lowest of the 104 large towns we cover, with plug-ins at 8.3%, one of the highest. The A3, A23, A24 and A217 are among the main roads, and the nearest service area is Moto Heston on the M4, about 16 km away. In the 2021 Census, 20.2% of working residents in the council area drove to work, and only 1.3% travelled 30 km or more. There are 2,641 privately kept vans, 89.5% of them diesel. The London ULEZ covers the borough and can charge both cars and vans. Because a remap doesn't change a vehicle's emissions standard, it has no bearing on that charge.

name: Middlesbrough
intro: Only three of the 104 large towns we cover have a higher share of diesel cars than Middlesbrough. At the end of June 2026, 36.8% of the 60,140 privately kept cars in the Middlesbrough council area ran on diesel, and their number fell by just 3.2% over the year, one of the smallest drops in the group. That makes diesel the obvious starting point for a Stage 1 remap here. The change is to the fuel, boost and timing settings, made in software and kept within the engine's limits. What you notice is mid-range torque, so the car pulls harder from lower revs and needs fewer changes down a gear.
driving: The A19, A66 and A174 are among Middlesbrough's main roads, and Teesside Truck Stop on the A66 is 4.7 km away. Neighbouring places are close: Eston is 4.3 km off, Thornaby-on-Tees 5 km and Billingham 6.6 km. In the 2021 Census, 54.8% of working residents in the Middlesbrough built-up area drove to work, well above the England and Wales figure of 45.1%, even though 33.3% of households had no car. In the council area, plug-ins are just 3.3% of private cars, one of the lowest shares of the 104, and 97.4% of the 3,392 private vans are diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across TS postcodes, the Ford Transit led the diesel vans, with the Peugeot Partner in the top five. Loaded vans are where the extra torque is most useful.

name: Milton Keynes
intro: Milton Keynes households are well supplied with cars, yet relatively few people commute far. In the 2021 Census only 17.6% of households in the built-up area had no car, against 23.3% for England and Wales, while just 11.5% of working residents travelled 10 km or more, compared with 19% across England and Wales. The count was taken in a lockdown, so treat these as a guide. Even so, for many drivers here the case for Stage 1 remapping is less about the daily commute and more about longer trips, loaded holidays and towing, where a diesel's extra mid-range torque is easiest to feel.
driving: The M1 is the only motorway on the main road list, alongside the A5, A421, A422 and A509, and Newport Pagnell Services on the M1 is 5.2 km away. Bletchley is also 5.2 km off. The Milton Keynes council area had 140,422 privately kept cars at the end of June 2026, 28.9% diesel and 54.3% petrol, with plug-ins at 7.1%. Private diesel cars fell from 43,083 to 40,567 over the year. In 2025 MOT tests across MK postcodes, the Volkswagen Golf, BMW 3 Series and Mercedes-Benz C Class were the top three diesel cars, and the Ford Transit led the vans. There were 7,419 private vans, 94.8% diesel. For runs onto the M1, Stage 1 helps with joining and overtaking.

name: Newcastle upon Tyne

caz.name: Newcastle and Gateshead (Tyneside) Clean Air Zone
caz.scope: It covers part of central Newcastle and Gateshead, including the Tyne crossings, and charges vans, not private cars.

intro: The Tyneside Clean Air Zone, covering part of Newcastle and Gateshead including the Tyne crossings, is a Class C charging zone: vans are charged, private cars are not. That split matters most to van owners. A remap leaves a vehicle's emissions standard as it was, so a van the zone charges today is charged after Stage 1 remapping too. The gain is in how the van handles weight: more mid-range torque for pulling away loaded, fewer downshifts on hills and less effort with a trailer, within the limits of the gearbox and clutch. Car drivers get the same kind of pull in everyday driving, with nothing bolted on.
driving: The A1 and A69 are among Newcastle's main roads, with the A167(M), A167, A184 and A696, and Seaton Burn Services on the A19 is 7.5 km away. In the 2021 Census, 37.2% of households in the Newcastle upon Tyne built-up area had no car, and 38.1% of working residents drove to work. In the council area, privately kept diesel cars fell from 34,036 to 32,298 in the year to June 2026, leaving diesel at 32% of private cars, and 95.9% of the 5,425 private vans were diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across NE postcodes, the Volkswagen Golf and Nissan Qashqai were the most tested diesel cars, and the Ford Transit led the vans ahead of the Volkswagen Transporter and Citroen Berlingo. On the A1, a remap mostly helps with overtaking.

name: Newham
intro: Most households in Newham had no car at the 2021 Census: 51.7% across the council area, more than double the England and Wales figure of 23.3%. Only 17.3% of working residents drove to work. Across E postcodes, the 2025 MOT figures lean towards big saloons: the Mercedes-Benz E Class was the most tested diesel car, ahead of the BMW 5 Series. For the households that do run a car like that, Stage 1 remapping makes it more relaxed to drive, with more mid-range torque for overtaking and joining fast roads. A remap must be declared to your insurer, and any fault is repaired before the work.
driving: Diesel cars are holding steady in the Newham council area. Their number fell only 1.5% in the year to June 2026, from 11,809 to 11,637, and no town among the 104 we cover recorded a smaller fall. Plug-ins make up 8.1% of private cars, one of the highest shares of the 104, while vans are scarce at 39 for every 1,000 private cars, one of the lowest ratios. The M11, A117 and A1020 are among the main roads. In 2025 MOT tests across E postcodes, the Ford Transit was the most tested diesel van and the Mercedes-Benz Vito the third. The ULEZ covers the borough and can charge cars and vans, and a remap doesn't change the emissions standard it checks.

name: Newport
intro: Nearly half the cars and small vans given an MOT across NP postcodes in 2025 were diesel: 45.9%. That covers the whole postcode area rather than Newport alone, but the council figures point the same way, with 33.1% of the 77,340 privately kept cars in the Newport council area running on diesel at the end of June 2026. For all those diesel owners, a Stage 1 remap is about the mid-range. The result you feel is torque at everyday revs, the kind that helps with a full boot, a trailer or a long climb, all from a change to the engine's software rather than its hardware.
driving: The M4 and A48(M) are both among Newport's main roads, and the three nearest listed service areas are all on the M4, the closest being Cardiff Gate at 10 km and Magor at 11.5 km. Cwmbrân is 7.6 km away and Cardiff 15.8 km. In the 2021 Census, 52.2% of working residents in the Newport built-up area drove to work and 20.5% travelled 10 km or more, both above the England and Wales figures of 45.1% and 19%. The council area has 5,773 private vans, 75 for every 1,000 private cars, and 95.9% are diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across NP postcodes, the Ford Transit was the most tested diesel van and the Volkswagen Golf the most tested diesel car. Gearbox and clutch limits matter on any van remap.

name: Northampton
intro: Diesel still made up 42.4% of the cars and small vans given an MOT at test stations across NN postcodes in 2025, and the Volkswagen Golf was the most tested diesel car, with 6,211. In the West Northamptonshire council area, 33.3% of the 227,114 privately kept cars were diesel at the end of June 2026. That is a lot of diesel engines, and on a diesel the gain from Stage 1 remapping is mid-range torque: easier overtaking, joining the M1 with less effort, and steadier pulling with a trailer. It is a software change to fuel, boost and timing, kept within the engine's limits, with nothing bolted on.
driving: Northampton Services on the M1 is 4.6 km away, and Red Lion Truckstop, also on the M1, is 7.5 km. The A43, A45, A428 and A508 are on the main road list too. In the 2021 Census, 50.3% of working residents in the Northampton built-up area drove to work, above 45.1% for England and Wales, and 4.9% travelled 30 km or more. The council area had 17,487 privately kept vans in June 2026, 77 for every 1,000 cars and 94.3% diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across NN postcodes, the Ford Transit led the diesel vans, followed by the Volkswagen Transporter. For a van running loaded on the M1, Stage 1 torque helps, provided the clutch and gearbox are in good health.

name: Norwich
intro: Petrol and diesel still power almost every private car in Norwich. Plug-ins are just 2.9% of privately kept cars in the Norwich council area, the second lowest share of the 104 large towns we cover, while 58.4% run on petrol and 32.8% on diesel. Those engines are what Stage 1 remapping works on. The remap is a software change to the fuel, boost and timing settings, kept within the engine's limits, with nothing bolted on. On a diesel the benefit you feel is mid-range torque, which takes the effort out of overtaking and pulling with a load. Changes in fuel use are modest and depend on how you drive.
driving: Thickthorn Services on the A11 is 6 km from Norwich, but the next nearest service areas are 56.6 km and 61.6 km away. The A11, A47 and A140 are among the main roads. Taverham and Drayton is 6.6 km away, Wymondham 13.7 km and Dereham 23.1 km. In the 2021 Census, 42.4% of working residents in the Norwich built-up area drove to work. Privately kept diesel cars in the council area fell only 3.3% over the year to June 2026, one of the smallest falls of the 104 large towns we cover. In 2025 MOT tests across NR postcodes, the Volkswagen Golf and Nissan Qashqai were the most tested diesel cars, and the Ford Transit led the vans. On long A-road runs, a remap's mid-range torque makes overtaking easier.

name: Nottingham
intro: Trent Bridge Services, on the A6011, is under 4 km from Nottingham, and two more service areas lie within 8 km: Trowell on the M1 and Pierrepont on the A52. Diesel is common here: 34.1% of privately kept cars in the Nottingham council area run on it, the 13th highest share of the 104 large towns we cover. On a diesel, Stage 1 remapping is felt as mid-range torque, which shows when joining the M1 from a slip road, passing a slow lorry on the A52 or climbing without changing down. Your insurer must be told, and a car with a fault is repaired before any remap.
driving: In the 2021 Census, 38.3% of working residents in the Nottingham built-up area drove to work, and the same share of households, 38.3%, had no car, against 23.3% across England and Wales. Arnold, West Bridgford and Beeston are all within about 6 km. The council area has 6,283 privately kept vans, 95.8% of them diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across NG postcodes, the Ford Transit was the most tested diesel van by a long way, at 11,282, with the Volkswagen Transporter and Vauxhall Vivaro next, while the Volkswagen Golf and Ford Focus led the diesel cars. For a van, a remap adds torque for loads and towing, within the limits of the gearbox and clutch.

name: Oldham
intro: High ground shapes driving in Oldham, which stands on elevated land among the Pennines. Hills are where a diesel shows what its mid-range is worth, and that is the part of the rev range a Stage 1 remap works on. Nothing is added to the engine; only its settings change, within its limits. The result is more pull from lower revs, so a car or loaded van holds its gear on a climb instead of changing down. At the end of June 2026, 30.4% of the 95,903 privately kept cars in the Oldham council area were diesel, along with 96.5% of its 6,232 private vans.
driving: Neighbouring towns are packed close: Lees is 2.6 km away, Royton 3.4 km and Chadderton 3.6 km. The M60 and A627(M) are among Oldham's main roads, with the A62 and A663, and the nearest listed service area is Moto Birch on the M62, 9.1 km away. In the 2021 Census, 50.7% of working residents in the Oldham built-up area drove to work, above the England and Wales figure of 45.1%, while 35% of households had no car. Private diesel cars in the council area fell from 30,944 to 29,196 over the year. In 2025 MOT tests across OL postcodes, the Volkswagen Golf led the diesel cars, with the Audi A3 in the top five, and the Ford Transit and Mercedes-Benz Sprinter led the vans.

name: Oxford

caz.name: Oxford Zero Emission Zone
caz.scope: It is a pilot covering a few city-centre streets and charges any vehicle that is not zero emission.

intro: A pilot Zero Emission Zone on streets in Oxford city centre, including New Road, Bonn Square, Ship Street and St Michael's Street, charges a daily fee to any car or van that is not zero emission. Away from those streets, Stage 1 remapping is about how the engine drives: a software change to fuel, boost and timing, within its limits, that gives a diesel more mid-range torque on the A34 and A40. Your insurer needs to know about it. What a remap can't do is change a vehicle's emissions standard, so a petrol or diesel car is charged in the pilot zone with or without one.
driving: Peartree Services on the A44 is 4.6 km away and Welcome Break Oxford Services on the M40 is 11.3 km. In the 2021 Census, 23.8% of working residents in the Oxford built-up area drove to work, against 45.1% for England and Wales, and 31.2% of households had no car. Diesel made up 29.1% of the 46,383 privately kept cars in the council area at the end of June 2026. In 2025 MOT tests across OX postcodes, 40% of cars and small vans tested were diesel; the Volkswagen Golf and Land Rover Discovery were the top two diesel cars, and the Ford Transit and Volkswagen Transporter the top vans. For a Discovery that tows, Stage 1 torque is the useful part.

name: Peterborough
intro: No large town we cover has a higher diesel share than Peterborough. At the end of June 2026, 40.3% of privately kept cars in the Peterborough council area were diesel, the highest of the 104, with petrol at 47.7%. That is 38,732 diesel cars. What Stage 1 remapping offers is aimed squarely at engines like these: more mid-range torque, which makes overtaking and joining the A1(M) easier and cuts down on downshifts. It is done in software, changing the fuel, boost and timing settings within the engine's limits, with nothing bolted on.
driving: The A1 and A1(M) are both among Peterborough's main roads, with the A15, A16, A47 and A605. Kate's Cabin on the A1 is 5.7 km away, Peterborough Services on the A1(M) 6.1 km and the Stibbington Diner lorry park 9.3 km. In the 2021 Census, 5.7% of working residents in the Peterborough built-up area travelled 30 km or more to work, above the England and Wales figure of 4.4%, and 48.1% drove. In 2025 MOT tests across PE postcodes, 47.7% of the cars and small vans tested were diesel, and the Ford Transit was the most tested diesel van, ahead of the Vauxhall Vivaro. On long A1 runs and with loaded vans, a remap's torque is the part you feel.

name: Poole
intro: If you run a van in Poole, you are far from alone. The Bournemouth, Christchurch and Poole council area has 97 privately kept vans for every 1,000 private cars, the 2nd highest ratio of the 104 large towns we cover, and 18,848 private vans in all, 94.2% of them diesel. For a van owner, Stage 1 remapping is mainly about torque. With a full load or a trailer behind, the extra mid-range pull means fewer gear changes and less labouring on hills. The clutch and gearbox set the ceiling, and a sensible remap stays below it. Insurers must be told.
driving: One detail stands out in 2025 MOT tests across BH postcodes: more Volkswagen Transporters than Ford Transits were tested among diesel vans, 6,934 against 6,037. The Volkswagen Golf led the diesel cars. The A35, A338, A348 and A350 are among the main roads, and the nearest service area, Picket Post on the A31, is about 21 km away. In the 2021 Census, 50% of working residents in the Poole built-up area drove to work and 40.8% of households had two or more cars, both above the England and Wales figures of 45.1% and 35.4%. Diesel makes up 27.5% of private cars in the council area, and on those a remap is felt as easier overtaking and stronger pull on hills.

name: Portsmouth
intro: Just 3% of the 77,505 privately kept cars in the Portsmouth council area are plug-ins, one of the lowest shares among the 104 large towns we cover. Vans, on the other hand, are unusually common: 7,030 privately kept, or 91 for every 1,000 private cars, the joint 5th highest ratio in the same group. Figures are for the end of June 2026. Petrol and diesel still dominate here, with a large private van fleet alongside them. A Stage 1 remap suits both in different ways: on a car it brings smoother, stronger pull in the middle of the rev range, and on a van it is the extra torque you feel when loaded or towing, set with the clutch and gearbox in mind.
driving: Farlington Services on the A27 is 2.8 km away, and the M275, M27 and A3(M) are also among Portsmouth's main roads. Gosport is 5.9 km from the city, Waterlooville 6.9 km and Havant 7.3 km. In the 2021 Census, 42.6% of working residents in the Portsmouth built-up area drove to work and only 12.2% travelled 10 km or more, against 19% across England and Wales, while 29.1% of households had no car. In the council area, diesel makes up 28.9% of private cars and 94.8% of private vans. In 2025 MOT tests across PO postcodes, the Ford Transit and Volkswagen Transporter were the most tested diesel vans, and the Volkswagen Golf the most tested diesel car. On a diesel, extra mid-range torque helps most on the M27 and A27.

name: Reading
intro: Behind the Volkswagen Golf, the Land Rover Discovery was the second most tested diesel car in 2025 MOT tests across RG postcodes, with 4,758 vehicles. If a Discovery or something like it is your tow car, Stage 1 remapping is mostly about what happens in the middle of the rev range: a stronger pull when moving off with weight behind, and fewer downshifts on a climb. The settings changed are fuel, boost and timing, all in software and inside the engine's limits, and your insurer has to be told. The RG count covers the whole postcode area, with the BMW 3 Series and Mercedes-Benz E Class next in line.
driving: The M4 and the A329(M) are the motorways on Reading's main road list, with the A33, A4 and A329 among the A roads, and Moto Reading Services on the M4 is 5.3 km away. Caversham is 4 km off and Woodley 4.4 km. In the 2021 Census, 34.3% of working residents in the built-up area drove to work, below 45.1% for England and Wales, and 25% of households had no car. The Reading council area had 66,234 privately kept cars at the end of June 2026, 26.8% diesel and 60.1% petrol, and 4,074 private vans, 95.1% diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across RG postcodes, the Ford Transit led the diesel vans. For a car that joins the M4 often, the extra mid-range torque is the part you notice.

name: Redbridge
intro: One in five working residents of the Redbridge council area travelled 10 km or more to work in the 2021 Census: 20.2%, a little above the England and Wales figure of 19%. Longer runs on the A12, A406 or M11 suit a remapped diesel: with Stage 1 remapping, the extra mid-range torque makes joining fast traffic and overtaking less of an effort, and the car needs fewer downshifts. The change is to the engine's fuel, boost and timing settings, kept within its limits, and nothing is bolted on. Diesel was 17.2% of privately kept cars in the council area at the end of June 2026, with petrol hybrids on 13.7%.
driving: London's ULEZ covers Redbridge and every other London borough, but not the M25, and it charges cars and vans by the day. A remap does not change a vehicle's emissions standard. Vans are relatively scarce here: 36 privately kept vans per 1,000 private cars at the end of June 2026, one of the lowest ratios of the 104 large towns we cover, though 93.2% of the 3,539 vans were diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across IG postcodes, the Mercedes-Benz E Class, BMW 5 Series and Mercedes-Benz C Class were the most tested diesel cars, and the Ford Transit led the vans. Chigwell is 3.5 km away, and the nearest service area, Thurrock on the M25, is 17 km. On a big saloon, Stage 1 mainly brings easier overtaking.

name: Richmond upon Thames
intro: At 8.9%, the plug-in share of privately kept cars in Richmond upon Thames is higher than in all but seven of the 104 large towns we cover. Diesel sits at 12.7%, one of the lowest shares, and petrol, at 68.1%, is the main fuel by far. For the petrol and diesel cars that make up most of the borough's total, Stage 1 remapping adjusts fuel, boost and timing in software, within the engine's limits, for a stronger, smoother mid-range. In London it also helps to be clear that a remap doesn't change a vehicle's emissions standard, so it won't change whether the ULEZ, which covers every London borough, charges a car.
driving: In the 2021 Census, only 17.5% of working residents in the Richmond upon Thames council area drove to work, and just 1.1% travelled 30 km or more. Vans are scarce, with 31 for every 1,000 private cars, among the lowest ratios of the 104, and of the 2,210 privately kept vans, 85.3% are diesel. Moto Heston Services on the M4 is about 7 km away, and Cobham Services on the M25 about 15 km, with the A316 and A308 among the main roads. In 2025 MOT tests across TW postcodes, the Mercedes-Benz E Class and C Class and the Land Rover Discovery were the most tested diesel cars. On cars that size, a remap mainly means easier overtaking and a more relaxed mid-range.

name: Rochdale
intro: The M62 is never far from Rochdale. Moto Birch Services on it is 6.8 km away, and the A627(M) is also among the town's main roads. Of the 95,687 privately kept cars in the Rochdale council area at the end of June 2026, 31.6% were diesel, close to one in three. For a diesel that regularly joins the motorway, a Stage 1 remap gives stronger pull from lower revs, so merging into faster traffic and overtaking take less effort. None of it involves new parts, only the engine's own settings, kept within its limits. If your diesel has an AdBlue or EGR fault, that is fixed before the remap.
driving: Heywood is 5.1 km away and Littleborough 5.2 km, with Royton and Shaw both 5.8 km. Other main roads include the A58, A640 and A664. In the 2021 Census, 54.5% of working residents in the Rochdale built-up area drove to work, well above the England and Wales figure of 45.1%, and 31% of households had two or more cars. The council area also has 6,395 privately kept vans, 97% of them diesel. On a van, extra torque helps when loaded or towing, within gearbox and clutch limits. In 2025 MOT tests across OL postcodes, the Nissan Qashqai was the second most tested diesel car after the Volkswagen Golf, and the Ford Transit Custom was third among the vans.

name: Salford
intro: The M602, M60 and A57(M) are all on Salford's main road list, and Manchester city centre lies just across the River Irwell. On that mix of motorway-standard roads and city streets, the part of a diesel's performance that Stage 1 remapping changes is the mid-range. You get more torque for joining the M60, overtaking and pulling away loaded, with fewer downshifts. The remap is a software adjustment to fuel, boost and timing, kept within the engine's limits. Fuel economy changes are modest and depend on how you drive, and any fault with the DPF, EGR or injectors is repaired before a remap.
driving: The closest listed service area is Moto Birch Services on the M62, 9.2 km away, and Old Trafford is 3.4 km off. In the 2021 Census, 44.3% of households in the Salford built-up area had no car, against 23.3% for England and Wales, and 30.6% of working residents drove to work. The Salford council area had 97,805 privately kept cars at the end of June 2026, 28.9% diesel and 57.9% petrol, and 5,889 private vans, 96.7% diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across M postcodes, the Volkswagen Golf led the diesel cars, and the Ford Transit and Mercedes-Benz Sprinter the vans. For a van that works across Greater Manchester, Stage 1 helps when loaded, within clutch and gearbox limits.

name: Sheffield

caz.name: Sheffield Clean Air Zone
caz.scope: It covers Sheffield city centre and the inner ring road and charges vans, not private cars.

intro: Hills come with the territory in Sheffield, which sits in the Don valley at the foot of the Pennines. The council area also counted 14,682 privately kept vans at the end of June 2026, and a loaded van on a climb is where Stage 1 remapping shows its value: more mid-range torque, fewer downshifts and easier pulling away with weight on board. The remap is a software change to the fuel, boost and timing settings, within the engine's limits, and the gearbox and clutch still set how far a van's remap can go. A van with an AdBlue, DPF or EGR fault is repaired first.
driving: Sheffield's Clean Air Zone, a Class C charging zone covering the city centre and inner ring road, charges vans but not private cars. A remap does not change a van's emissions standard, so the charge is unaffected. The M1 is among the main roads, with the A61, A57, A621 and A630, and the Sheffield Service Area on the A6102 is just 3 km away. In the 2021 Census, 43.9% of working residents in the Sheffield built-up area drove to work and 30.6% of households had no car. Diesel was 32.6% of private cars in the council area and 95.3% of private vans. In 2025 MOT tests across S postcodes, the Ford Transit was by far the most tested diesel van, and the Volkswagen Golf and Ford Focus led the cars.

name: Slough
intro: The M4, M40 and M25 are all on Slough's main road list, and ExtraMSA Beaconsfield Services on the M40 is about 8 km away. With three motorways nearby, many journeys can include a motorway stretch, and that is where a diesel's mid-range matters: joining from a slip road and pulling past slower traffic. Stage 1 remapping improves exactly that part of the engine's response. It changes fuel, boost and timing in software, inside the engine's limits, with no hardware added. Fuel use may shift a little either way depending on how you drive, so the reason to remap is drivability, not savings. Your insurer must be told.
driving: In the 2021 Census, 46.3% of working residents in the Slough built-up area drove to work and 17.9% travelled 10 km or more. Car ownership was high: 38.3% of households had two or more cars, above the England and Wales figure of 35.4%, and only 19.6% had none. Diesel makes up 26% of the 64,633 privately kept cars in the council area, down 6.4% in a year. There are 3,017 privately kept vans, 96.5% of them diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across SL postcodes, the Volkswagen Golf was the most tested diesel car, narrowly ahead of the Mercedes-Benz E Class, and the Ford Transit led the vans. A remapped Transit carries a load more easily, within its gearbox and clutch limits.

name: Solihull
intro: Households with two or more cars made up 45.3% of all households in the Solihull built-up area in the 2021 Census, against 35.4% across England and Wales, and only 15.1% of households had no car. With more than one car on the drive, it is worth choosing which one a Stage 1 remap suits: often the one doing the longer runs or the towing. The remap is a software change to the fuel, boost and timing settings, kept within the engine's limits, with nothing bolted on. On a diesel the gain you feel most is mid-range torque, for overtaking, joining faster roads and pulling a trailer.
driving: The M42, A34, A41 and A45 are among Solihull's main roads, and the nearest listed service areas are Hopwood Park on the M42 at 10.7 km and Moto Frankley on the M5 at 14.4 km. Birmingham is 8.8 km away. In the 2021 Census, 46.6% of working residents in the built-up area drove to work. Private diesel cars in the Solihull council area fell 7.3% in the year to June 2026, from 30,414 to 28,188, one of the steepest drops among the 104 large towns we cover, leaving diesel at 25.6% of 109,970 private cars. In 2025 MOT tests across B postcodes, the Volkswagen Golf was the most tested diesel car and the Ford Transit the most tested diesel van, ahead of the Mercedes-Benz Sprinter.

name: Southampton
intro: Combustion engines still power almost every car in the Southampton council area. Plug-ins accounted for 3.3% of privately kept cars there at the end of June 2026, one of the lowest shares of the 104 large towns we cover, while diesel stood at 30.8% and petrol at 57.8%. That is the ground Stage 1 remapping covers. It is a software change to fuel, boost and timing, within the engine's limits, and on a diesel you feel it as mid-range torque, useful when joining fast roads or overtaking. Fuel economy changes are modest and depend on driving style. Insurers must be told about a remap.
driving: The M27, M3 and M271 are all on the main road list, with the A33, A35 and A335, and Rownhams Services on the M27 is 5.8 km away. Hedge End is 6.1 km off and Eastleigh 6.5 km. Vans matter here: the council area had 7,988 privately kept vans in June 2026, 83 for every 1,000 cars, the 10th highest of the 104 towns, and 95.5% were diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across SO postcodes, the Ford Transit and Volkswagen Transporter led the diesel vans. In the 2021 Census, 43.7% of working residents in the built-up area drove to work. For a van that spends its day loaded, Stage 1 torque helps, as long as the clutch and gearbox are sound.

name: Southend-on-Sea
intro: The Ford Kuga was the most tested diesel car in 2025 MOT tests across SS postcodes, with 4,723 vehicles, almost double the Ford Focus on 2,528. Ford also took the top three places among diesel vans: Transit, Transit Custom and Transit Connect. A family SUV like the Kuga carrying passengers, luggage or a trailer, and a Transit loaded for work, both lean on mid-range torque, and that is what Stage 1 remapping adds on a diesel, along with fewer downshifts. It is a software change to the fuel, boost and timing settings, within the engine's limits, and on a van the gearbox and clutch limits still apply.
driving: The closest service area to Southend-on-Sea is Orsett Cock on the A13, 21.1 km away, with Moto Medway on the M2 at 24.6 km. The main roads include the A127 and A13, with the A1158, A1159, A1015 and A1160. In the 2021 Census, 6.8% of working residents in the Southend-on-Sea built-up area travelled 30 km or more to work, above the England and Wales figure of 4.4%, and 39.8% drove to work. Rochford is 3.5 km away and Rayleigh 8 km. In the council area, 22.8% of privately kept cars were diesel at the end of June 2026, and there were 72 private vans for every 1,000 cars. On longer A127 and A13 trips, a remap's torque makes overtaking easier.

name: Southwark
intro: Very few working residents in Southwark drove to work in the 2021 Census: 8.8% across the council area, against 45.1% for England and Wales. A clear majority of households, 60.3%, had no car at all. Of the 50,991 privately kept cars at the end of June 2026, plug-ins make up 8%, one of the highest shares of the 104 large towns we cover. Stage 1 remapping here is a choice for the minority who drive, and what it changes is the mid-range: a firmer response, easier overtaking and fewer downshifts, with the car's hardware left as it is. Your insurer must be told about it.
driving: Diesel is 13.1% of private cars in the council area, one of the lowest shares of the 104, and petrol 69.6%, so the remap question here is often about a petrol car, where the same software approach gives a smoother, stronger response. In the 2021 Census, only 6.5% of households in the council area had two or more cars, and 6.3% of working residents travelled 10 km or more. Of the 2,111 privately kept vans, 85% are diesel. The A100, A202 and A3204 are among the borough's main roads, and the nearest service area is London Gateway on the M1, about 21 km away. The ULEZ covers the borough and can charge cars and vans. A remap doesn't change a vehicle's emissions standard, so it doesn't change the charge.

name: St Helens
intro: St Helens is a driving town. In the 2021 Census, 57.1% of working residents in the St Helens built-up area drove to work, well above the England and Wales figure of 45.1%. For a daily driver, a Stage 1 remap is about making that routine easier. On a diesel, the gain shows in the mid-range, so the car feels less laboured at the revs you use every day and joining faster roads takes less effort. Any fault, such as a DPF or EGR problem, is repaired first, and your insurer must be told about the remap.
driving: The M62 and M57 are both among St Helens' main roads, and two motorway service areas are close: Earlsfield on the M57 at 6.3 km and Burtonwood on the M62 at 7.3 km. Prescot is 4.7 km away and Haydock 5 km. Of the 85,609 privately kept cars in the St Helens council area at the end of June 2026, 29.5% were diesel, and the council area also had 6,011 private vans, 70 for every 1,000 cars, 97% of them diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across WA postcodes, the Ford Kuga was the most tested diesel car and the Ford Transit the most tested diesel van. A van owner here would feel the gain most on a loaded run, within what the clutch and gearbox allow.

name: Stockport
intro: One of the sharper falls in diesel cars came in the Stockport council area. A year before the end of June 2026 there were 39,016 privately kept diesel cars; by then there were 36,268, a fall of 7% and the 12th biggest of the 104 large towns we cover. Even so, diesel still made up 25.5% of the 142,018 private cars there. On one of those diesels, Stage 1 remapping adds mid-range torque, the pull you use when overtaking or climbing, through software changes to fuel, boost and timing within the engine's limits. Fault first, remap second: a DPF, AdBlue or EGR problem is repaired before anything else.
driving: Three motorways, the M60, M56 and M67, are on Stockport's main road list, with the A6, A560 and A34, yet the nearest listed service area, Moto Birch Services on the M62, is 18.1 km away. Reddish is 3.6 km off and Cheadle 4 km. In the 2021 Census, 44.3% of working residents in the built-up area drove to work and only 1.9% travelled 30 km or more. The council area's 8,904 private vans were 94.9% diesel at the end of June 2026. In 2025 MOT tests across SK postcodes, the Volkswagen Golf and Land Rover Discovery were the top two diesel cars and the Ford Transit led the vans. With short commutes and the M60 on the list, joining it is where Stage 1 torque shows.

name: Stoke-on-Trent
intro: Driving to work was the norm in Stoke-on-Trent at the 2021 Census: 58.3% of working residents in the built-up area did so, well above the England and Wales figure of 45.1%. On a daily commute, Stage 1 remapping is about how the car drives rather than how fast it can go. It is a software change to the fuel, boost and timing settings, kept within the engine's limits. On a diesel you notice the mid-range torque: easier joins onto fast roads, less need to change down and calmer overtaking. Any change in fuel use depends on how you drive and is modest, and your insurer must be told.
driving: Diesel was 33.6% of privately kept cars in the Stoke-on-Trent council area at the end of June 2026, and there were 78 private vans for every 1,000 cars, both the 15th highest of the 104 large towns we cover. Plug-ins were just 3.6%, one of the lowest shares. The M6, A50 and A500 are among the main roads, Swift Services on the M6 is 4.9 km away and Keele Services 9.3 km, and Newcastle-under-Lyme is 7.3 km off. In 2025 MOT tests across ST postcodes, the Ford Transit and Volkswagen Transporter were the most tested diesel vans and the Volkswagen Golf led the cars. For a loaded van on the A500 or M6, extra torque helps with merging, within what the gearbox and clutch can take.

name: Sunderland
intro: Close to a third of privately kept cars in the Sunderland council area are diesel: 33.7% at the end of June 2026, the 14th highest share of the 104 large towns we cover. That comes to 39,353 diesel cars in private hands. For those drivers, the case for Stage 1 remapping rests on mid-range torque: overtaking and joining faster roads take less effort, and the car needs fewer downshifts. It is software only, with the engine's limits respected. Fuel use may change slightly, depending on how you drive. If the car has a DPF, EGR or injector fault, that is repaired first.
driving: In 2025 MOT tests across SR postcodes, the Nissan Qashqai was the most tested diesel car, just ahead of the Volkswagen Golf, and the Ford Transit led the diesel vans. The council area has 8,533 privately kept vans, 96.7% of them diesel. In the 2021 Census, 50.3% of working residents in the Sunderland built-up area drove to work, above the England and Wales figure of 45.1%, and 34.1% of households had no car. Moto Washington Services on the A1(M) is about 10 km away and Easington Services on the A19 about 12 km, with the A19 and A1231 among the main roads. On a Qashqai, a remap gives easier, more relaxed pull on the A19.

name: Sutton
intro: Sutton has the lowest diesel share of the 104 large towns we cover. At the end of June 2026, just 11.8% of the 81,150 privately kept cars in the Sutton council area ran on diesel, against 70.3% on petrol. That changes the usual Stage 1 remap conversation. Here, petrol cars are the majority, and on a petrol car the remap works on the same kind of fuel, boost and timing settings as it does on a diesel, in software and within the engine's limits. Sutton's diesel drivers, a small group, will notice the extra mid-range torque most when overtaking.
driving: No motorway appears among Sutton's main roads, which include the A217, A232, A24 and A23. The nearest listed service areas, Cobham and Clacket Lane, are both on the M25, at 17.2 km and 17.7 km. In the 2021 Census, 34.6% of working residents in the Sutton council area drove to work, below the England and Wales figure of 45.1%, and 30.2% of households had two or more cars. The council area has 4,043 private vans, 91.3% diesel, and in 2025 MOT tests across SM postcodes the Ford Transit led the diesel vans, with the Renault Trafic in the top five. Sutton is within the ULEZ, which can charge cars and vans daily. A remap does not change a vehicle's emissions standard, so it cannot change whether the ULEZ charges it.

name: Swansea
intro: Vans matter more in Swansea than anywhere else in our list of 104 large towns. At the end of June 2026 the Swansea council area had 12,814 privately kept vans, 105 for every 1,000 private cars, the highest ratio of the 104, and 96.6% of them were diesel. So any honest look at Stage 1 remapping here starts with vans. With weight on board, a diesel van gains most in the mid-range: it pulls away more easily, holds speed on a gradient and needs fewer gear changes when towing. Clutch and gearbox limits still apply, and a sensible remap respects them.
driving: The M4 is on the main road list with the A483, A465 and A48, and Moto Swansea West Services on the M4 is 5.9 km away, with Pont Abraham Services 14.8 km. In the 2021 Census, 54% of working residents in the Swansea built-up area drove to work, well above 45.1% for England and Wales. Diesel made up 31.4% of the council area's 122,252 privately kept cars in June 2026. In 2025 MOT tests across SA postcodes, 48% of cars and small vans tested were diesel; the Ford Transit and Volkswagen Transporter led the vans and the Volkswagen Golf the cars. From the roads of the Gower to the M4, a diesel with good mid-range pull is easier work.

name: Swindon
intro: Swindon sits on the M4 corridor, and the M4 is the motorway on its list of main roads, with the A419, A420 and A4311 alongside. For a car that spends its week on the M4, Stage 1 remapping is less about pace from a standstill and more about response at motorway speed: a diesel's extra mid-range torque lets it hold a higher gear and overtake without a downshift. The remap changes the fuel, boost and timing settings, within the engine's limits, and nothing is bolted on. Fuel economy changes depend on how the car is driven and are modest. Your insurer must be told, and a vehicle with a DPF, EGR or AdBlue fault is repaired first.
driving: Vans are common: the Swindon council area had 80 privately kept vans per 1,000 private cars at the end of June 2026, the 12th highest ratio of the 104 large towns we cover, and 95.8% of the 9,225 vans were diesel. In the 2021 Census, 5.9% of working residents in the Swindon built-up area travelled 30 km or more to work, above the England and Wales figure of 4.4%, and 36.3% of households had two or more cars. The nearest service area is the Onroute truckstop at J15 on the A420, 4.7 km away. In 2025 MOT tests across SN postcodes, the Ford Transit and Volkswagen Transporter led the diesel vans, and the Volkswagen Golf and Land Rover Discovery the cars. A loaded Transporter gains most from extra torque.

name: Telford
intro: Over half of working residents in the Telford built-up area drove to work in the 2021 Census, 56.4%, well above the England and Wales figure of 45.1%, and 5.3% travelled 30 km or more. Diesel is common too: 35.9% of privately kept cars in the Telford and Wrekin council area, the 7th highest share of the 104 large towns we cover. For a diesel that regularly runs on the M54, Stage 1 remapping is felt in the mid-range: joining at speed and overtaking take less effort, and the car holds a gear on inclines. Fuel use may change a little, depending on how you drive.
driving: Vans are a strong part of the mix: the council area has 7,411 privately kept vans, 79 for every 1,000 private cars, one of the highest ratios of the 104, and 95.9% are diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across TF postcodes, the Ford Transit was the most tested diesel van with the Volkswagen Transporter second, and the Volkswagen Golf led the diesel cars. Two or more cars were kept by 37.8% of households in the built-up area in the 2021 Census. Telford Services is about 5 km away, and the A5, A442 and A518 are among the main roads. For a loaded van, a remap's torque helps on longer runs, within gearbox and clutch limits.

name: Tower Hamlets
intro: Vans are scarce among private vehicles in Tower Hamlets: 1,157 privately kept vans in the council area at the end of June 2026, or 27 for every 1,000 private cars, one of the lowest ratios among the 104 large towns we cover. Plug-ins, by contrast, make up 10.1% of the 42,504 private cars, the joint 4th highest share in the same group. That makes petrol and diesel cars, with diesel at 16.7%, the main candidates for a Stage 1 remap here. For those cars, the effect is felt in the mid-range, where stronger torque makes overtaking easier and cuts the number of downshifts.
driving: The A11, A12 and A13 are among Tower Hamlets' main roads, and the nearest listed service area, London Gateway on the M1, is 20.3 km away. Hackney is 4.1 km away. In the 2021 Census, 66.4% of households in the Tower Hamlets council area had no car, against 23.3% across England and Wales, and just 9.1% of working residents drove to work. Private diesel cars in the council area fell only 3.1% over the year to June 2026, one of the smallest falls of the 104. In 2025 MOT tests across E postcodes, the Mercedes-Benz E Class led the diesel cars. Inside the ULEZ, cars and vans can face a daily charge, and remapping one does not change that, because its emissions standard stays as it was.

name: Waltham Forest
intro: Diesel cars are leaving Waltham Forest's roads more slowly than almost anywhere else we cover. Privately kept diesel cars in the council area fell by only 2.5% in the year to June 2026, from 10,989 to 10,709, the 5th smallest fall of the 104 large towns in our list. A diesel that is staying on the road for a few more years is a fair candidate for Stage 1 remapping, provided it is healthy: any DPF, EGR or injector fault is repaired first. Fuel, boost and timing settings are then changed in software, within the engine's limits, and the gain is mid-range torque for overtaking and joining faster roads.
driving: Waltham Forest is inside the London Ultra Low Emission Zone, which can charge cars and vans daily, and a remap won't change a vehicle's emissions standard or its ULEZ position. The M11, A12 and A406 are on the main road list, but the nearest listed service area, London Gateway Services on the M1, is 18.4 km away. In the 2021 Census, 19.6% of working residents in the council area drove to work and 42.1% of households had no car. Petrol made up 67.1% of the 70,139 private cars in June 2026 and petrol hybrids 11.4%. In 2025 MOT tests across E postcodes, the Mercedes-Benz E Class and BMW 5 Series led the diesel cars, and the Ford Transit the vans.

name: Wandsworth
intro: London's Ultra Low Emission Zone covers every London borough, Wandsworth included, and charges both cars and vans by the day. Plug-ins already make up 8.8% of privately kept cars in the Wandsworth council area, the 9th highest share of the 104 large towns we cover, though petrol, on 67.4%, is still the main fuel. For the cars that still run on petrol or diesel, Stage 1 remapping is a software change to the fuel, boost and timing settings, within the engine's limits. It does not touch the emissions standard, so the ULEZ treats a remapped car exactly as before.
driving: The A3 and A24 are among the borough's main roads, with the A205, A214 and A217, and the nearest service area, Moto Heston on the M4, is 15.4 km away. In the 2021 Census, 47.9% of households in the Wandsworth council area had no car and 9.3% of working residents drove to work. Vans are few: 31 privately kept vans per 1,000 private cars at the end of June 2026, one of the lowest ratios of the 104 large towns we cover, and only 84.5% of the 2,213 vans were diesel. Diesel cars fell from 10,084 to 9,511 over the year. Lambeth is 4.6 km away and Merton 4.8 km. For short trips across Inner London, a remap mainly makes a car feel more responsive when pulling away.

name: Warrington
intro: Diesel's decline has been sharp in Warrington. Over the year to June 2026, the number of privately kept diesel cars in the council area fell from 33,244 to 30,673, a 7.7% drop and one of the steepest of the 104 large towns we cover. Diesel now makes up 27.8% of private cars. A shrinking diesel count doesn't change what Stage 1 remapping does for the cars still on the road: more mid-range torque, so joining a motorway or overtaking takes less effort. It doesn't change a car's emissions standard either. Your insurer must be told about it.
driving: The M62, M6 and M56 are all on Warrington's main road list, and Burtonwood Services on the M62 is about 5 km away, with Lymm Services on the M6 about 6 km. In the 2021 Census, 51.5% of working residents in the Warrington built-up area drove to work and 39.1% of households had two or more cars, both above the England and Wales figures of 45.1% and 35.4%. The council area has 7,083 privately kept vans, 96.3% diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across WA postcodes, the Ford Kuga was the most tested diesel car, narrowly ahead of the Ford Focus, and the Ford Transit led the diesel vans. On motorway runs, the extra mid-range torque makes a loaded van easier to keep at pace, within gearbox and clutch limits.

name: Watford
intro: Down 7.5% in a year: that is the fall in privately kept diesel cars in the Watford council area, from 9,150 to 8,468 in the year to June 2026, and one of the steepest drops among the 104 large towns we cover. Diesel now makes up 19.9% of the 42,631 private cars, with petrol at 63%. For a diesel or a petrol car alike, a Stage 1 remap means new engine settings rather than new parts, set within the engine's limits. On a diesel, it is mid-range torque you would notice, with the car holding a higher gear for longer instead of changing down.
driving: The M1 and M25 are both among Watford's main roads, with the A41 and A405, and London Gateway Services on the M1 is 9.8 km away. Bushey is 3.3 km from Watford and Rickmansworth 4.2 km. In the 2021 Census, 40.1% of working residents in the Watford built-up area drove to work and 35.3% of households had two or more cars, close to the England and Wales figure of 35.4%. The council area has 2,215 private vans, 94.8% diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across WD postcodes, the Mercedes-Benz E Class was the most tested diesel car and the Ford Transit the most tested diesel van. A van remap has to respect the gearbox and clutch as well as the engine. Any remap must be declared to your insurer.

name: West Bromwich
intro: Sandwell, the council area that includes West Bromwich, had one of the highest diesel shares of the 104 large towns we cover at the end of June 2026: 33.6% of its 135,655 privately kept cars, the 15th highest. Plug-in cars made up only 3.3%, one of the lowest shares. For the owner of one of those diesels, Stage 1 remapping is felt in the mid-range: overtaking takes less effort and a trailer feels lighter on a climb. Fuel, boost and timing settings are adjusted in software and kept within the engine's limits, and any DPF, EGR or AdBlue fault is repaired first.
driving: The M5 and M6 are both on the main road list, with the A41, A34 and A4123, and Moto Frankley Services on the M5 is 11.4 km away. Wednesbury is 3.4 km off, Oldbury 4.1 km and Smethwick 4.4 km. In the 2021 Census, 52.5% of working residents in the West Bromwich built-up area drove to work, above 45.1% for England and Wales. Sandwell's 8,654 private vans were 96.8% diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across B postcodes, the Ford Transit led the diesel vans with 14,746, closely followed by the Mercedes-Benz Sprinter with 13,001, and the Volkswagen Golf led the cars. For a loaded Sprinter or Transit, Stage 1 torque helps within clutch and gearbox limits.

name: Wolverhampton
intro: Of the 7,178 privately kept vans in the Wolverhampton council area at the end of June 2026, 97% ran on diesel. Cars lean the same way: 35.3% of private cars there were diesel, the 9th highest share of the 104 large towns we cover. For a diesel van or car, Stage 1 remapping is a software change to the fuel, boost and timing settings, within the engine's limits, with nothing bolted on. What changes on the road is mid-range torque: easier pulling away with a load, fewer downshifts and more relaxed overtaking. On a van, the gearbox and clutch set the limits, and any DPF or EGR fault is repaired first.
driving: The M54 begins north of the city and links it with Telford, and Moto Hilton Park Services on the M6 is 8 km away. Other main roads include the A449, A41, A454, A460 and A4123. In the 2021 Census, 53.8% of working residents in the Wolverhampton built-up area drove to work, above the England and Wales figure of 45.1%, and 19.5% travelled 10 km or more. Bilston is 4.7 km away, with Willenhall and Codsall at 6 km. In 2025 MOT tests across WV postcodes, the Volkswagen Golf and BMW 3 Series were the most tested diesel cars, and the Ford Transit and Mercedes-Benz Sprinter led the vans. Joining the M54 or M6 is where a remap's extra torque is easiest to feel.

name: Worcester
intro: Only 20.3% of households in the Worcester built-up area had no car in the 2021 Census, below the England and Wales figure of 23.3%, and 37.4% had two or more, above the 35.4% for England and Wales. Cars are part of daily life for most households here, and 30.3% of the 51,507 privately kept cars in the Worcester council area run on diesel. For a diesel doing everyday family driving, Stage 1 remapping brings more mid-range torque: easier overtaking and fewer downshifts on hills. Tell your insurer about the remap, as you would with any change to the car's performance.
driving: Worcester's council area has 3,858 privately kept vans, 75 for every 1,000 private cars, and 94.6% of them are diesel. In 2025 MOT tests across WR postcodes, the Volkswagen Transporter was the most tested diesel van, ahead of the Ford Transit, and the Volkswagen Golf led the diesel cars, with the Land Rover Discovery second. In the 2021 Census, 6.1% of working residents in the built-up area travelled 30 km or more, above the England and Wales figure of 4.4%. RoadChef Strensham Services on the M5 is about 16 km away, and the A38, A44 and A4440 are among the main roads. For a Transporter carrying a load or towing, a remap's extra torque helps, within gearbox and clutch limits.

name: Worthing
intro: Without a motorway on its list of main roads, Worthing relies on A-roads such as the A27, A24 and A259. Vans are common here: the Worthing council area had 86 privately kept vans for every 1,000 private cars at the end of June 2026, the 9th highest ratio among the 104 large towns we cover. For a loaded van on roads like these, a Stage 1 remap helps most with pulling away and overtaking, because the gain is mid-range torque. The change is to the engine's software, inside its limits, with nothing bolted on, and the gearbox and clutch set how far it should go.
driving: The nearest listed service areas are Fontwell on the A27 at 17.6 km, Pyecombe on the A23 at 17.9 km and Buck Barn on the A24 at 18.6 km. Lancing and Sompting are 5.3 km away, Rustington 5.6 km and Shoreham-by-Sea 9.3 km. In the 2021 Census, 44.2% of working residents in the Worthing built-up area drove to work and 34% of households had two or more cars. Of the 53,131 private cars in the council area, 23.7% are diesel and 64.9% petrol. The 4,552 private vans are 93.3% diesel, and in 2025 MOT tests across BN postcodes the Ford Transit and Volkswagen Transporter were the most tested diesel vans. Your insurer needs to know about any remap.

name: York
intro: York's main road list runs to eight A roads and no motorway: the A64, A19, A59, A1079, A1237, A166, A1036 and A1176. The nearest listed service area, Bilbrough Top on the A64, is 8.5 km away. So Stage 1 remapping here is judged on A-road driving rather than motorway cruising: how easily a diesel overtakes, how it pulls away and whether it holds a gear on a rise. Those all come down to mid-range torque, which is what the remap's fuel, boost and timing changes add, within the engine's limits. Your insurer must be told about a remap.
driving: In the 2021 Census, 5.4% of working residents in the York built-up area travelled 30 km or more, above 4.4% for England and Wales, while 33.1% drove to work, below the 45.1% figure. Selby is 19.7 km away and Wetherby 19.8 km, and Moto Wetherby Services on the A1(M) is 18.4 km. In 2025 MOT tests across YO postcodes, 44.7% of cars and small vans tested were diesel, and the Land Rover Discovery was the second most tested diesel car behind the Volkswagen Golf. The York council area had 6,208 private vans at the end of June 2026, 95.6% diesel, and 28% of its 83,015 private cars were diesel. Longer A-road runs and towing are where Stage 1 torque pays off.
